title: Roma’s Perfect Start Ends With a Gut-Punch Draw Against Inter
description: Roma blows a two-goal lead against Inter, settling for a draw after a dominant first half gives way to a costly second.
fullText:
Led by a rejuvenated Paulo Dybala, the scorching-hot Donyell Malen, and an airtight defense that has conceded only one league goal, Roma has been playing some of the best football on the continent and has emerged as an early-season title contender. The only real criticism of Roma thus far has been the quality of the competition; it's one thing to wipe the floor with Lecce, but beating Inter is a different challenge altogether.

And it's a challenge that Roma and Gian Piero Gasperini have failed miserably at for, oh, the past decade. The last time Roma defeated Inter Milan at the Olimpico was October 2, 2016, while Gasperini has gone winless in his last 17 matches against the San Siro crew.

Despite those omens, Roma came out on the front foot in this fixture, relying on the same approach that worked so well against the Fiorentinas and Lecces of the world: control possession, counter-press high up the pitch, and stretch the defense with quick, intricate passing in the final third. It's practically page one of the Gasperini playbook, and while it served well against lesser clubs, there was no guarantee it would subdue mighty Inter Milan.

But thanks to the combined efforts of Dybala and Malen in attack and pressure from Manu Koné in midfield, Roma was in complete control early in this match, maintaining possession, winning 50/50s, and denying Inter a chance to build momentum. And just as they've done so many times early this season, Roma's leg work paid off with an early goal.

ROMA STRIKE EARLY 💥

Manu Kone finishes a wonderful move to put the Giallorossi ahead against Inter 🤩

Watch Serie A on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/EL1xLMCoQT

If there's one oft-heard criticism of Koné, it's his finishing. Inconsistent results in front of goal help explain why he's valued at €60 million rather than €80 million, but Koné showed exceptional technique here, getting a clean look at the ball even as it ran away from him. We'd also be remiss not to credit Molina, not only for the assist but also for wrangling the loose ball that started the play.

Holding a one-goal lead over any opponent is seldom a comfortable position, but against a side of Inter's quality, not to mention a penchant for overcoming deficits, it's downright anxiety-inducing. As the first half wore on, Inter grew increasingly adept at breaking the Roma press and creating scoring chances of their own, coming excruciatingly close to equalizing in the 26th minute, only to be denied by a scrambling Mile Svilar.

Inter were THIS 🤏 close to equalizing against Roma 😵

Mile Svilar is proving why he’s one of the best goalkeepers in Serie A 🇷🇸

Watch Serie A on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/DgKmtHlJCp

Still, despite Inter's interstitial awakening, Roma held statistical sway as the match crept toward intermission, holding nearly 60% of the ball and outshooting their visitors 10-3. The only thing that could have strengthened Roma's position was another goal before the break, and that's precisely what they received, thanks once again to Koné.

MANU KONÉ HAS SCORED TWICE AGAINST INTER 🔥

The French midfielder is doing it all himself as Roma go 2-0 up in this heavyweight Serie A clash 🐺

Watch Serie A on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/y0QTqYh9UG

While a semi-touch from Gianluca Mancini robbed him of an actual assist, Dybala planted the seeds of this goal with a delicately placed ball at the far post, practically dropping it in Koné's lap to pad Roma's heading into the break.

Unfortunately, Roma's joy was short-lived as Inter pulled one back almost immediately after the second half began.

GAME ON AT THE OLIMPICO 🤯

Lautaro Martínez pulls a goal back against Roma early in the second half 👀

Watch Serie A on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/pm4gPqIape

Starting with a Mancini turnover in midfield and conceding a goal despite outnumbering the opposition 5-2 in the box, this was a complete disaster for the Giallorossi. After losing possession (and his footing), Mancini failed to keep pace with Marcus Thuram down the left channel, setting the stage for a quick one-two goal between the Frenchman and Lautaro Martinez, who slotted the ball home amidst a thicket of four Roma defenders.

Despite seeing their lead halved in just 60 seconds, Roma stemmed the tide, ceding possession but doing enough to avoid a total disaster. With a one-goal lead to protect, Gasperini went heavy on defense in the second half, bringing on Evan Ndicka, Niccolo Pisilli and Devyne Rensch at the hour mark, before replacing the injured Leonardo Balerdi with Daniele Ghilardi in the 63rd minute.

Roma came close to regaining their two-goal lead in the 68th minute after Malen executed an impressive settle-turn-shoot move in the box, rifling a shot off Inter keeper Josep Martinez's face. This was Roma's last best chance, and while I'm not sure it qualifies as a save—he was otherwise beaten before the ball happened to hit his face—this stroke of luck loomed large in the final result.

Ten minutes later, Roma Happened…

LAUTARO MARTÍNEZ FIRES INTER BACK LEVEL 🔥

This Inter team just REFUSES to give up, we are level here at the Stadio Olimpico 🏟️

Watch Serie A on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/NY7VsarrY1

Similar to his first strike, Martinez found the tiniest crevice in Roma's defense, tucking in between multiple red shirts before beating Svilar at the far post. And that was all she wrote for the Giallorossi, who didn't manage a single attempt in the final 10 minutes plus stoppage.

Despite whatever disappointment we're feeling now, things aren't that bleak. With today's draw, Roma remain in first place, even on points with Inter Milan, though Lazio and Como may soon join them on 13 points. No, the real shame in today's results is twofold: First, they failed to create a three-point lead at the top of the table, an opportunity cost that could haunt them later this spring, but, perhaps more importantly, they failed a critical litmus test.

A victory today wouldn't have sewn up the Scudetto, but it would have been a clear and undeniable signal that Roma's title ambitions were legitimate. Reeling off five straight wins to begin the season, punctuated by a convincing victory over the defending champions before heading into the international break, would have been a tremendous shot in the arm for the Giallorossi.

The international break. Roma jumps back into action on October 11th when they face Como on the road.

title: Rosenior abused but guides Paris FC past old club Strasbourg
description: Paris FC extended their unbeaten start to the Ligue 1 campaign, beating coach Liam Rosenior's old charges Strasbourg 2-1 on Saturday in a match marred by abusive chants towards the Englishman from visiting fans.Monaco continued their own strong start in Ligue 1 with a 2-1 win over Lens on Friday.
fullText:
Paris FC extended their unbeaten start to the Ligue 1 campaign, beating coach Liam Rosenior's old charges Strasbourg 2-1 on Saturday in a match marred by abusive chants towards the Englishman from visiting fans.

The game was halted in the second half as Rosenior was targeted by his former supporters.

There were also ugly scenes after the final whistle as Rosenior motioned to remonstrate with the away fans and had to be pulled away by his players.

"I understand French, I knew what they were saying and they went too far. It's a great city and a great club, but there were many reasons for me to celebrate the way I did," Rosenior said after the game, adding that the provocation came from a small section of fans who had never wished him well.

Rosenior was brought back to France after a torrid time at Chelsea by Paris FC's multi-billionaire owners, the Arnault family, and has taken the team to second place in the early table behind Monaco.

Goals from Ilan Kebbal on 18 minutes and Pablo Pagis 12 minutes into the second half were enough for the capital club to add a third win to their two draws so far this campaign, despite conceding a late own goal by Moustapha Mbow.

Monaco continued their own strong start in Ligue 1 with a 2-1 win over Lens on Friday.

Lille and Rennes could join Monaco on 13 points when they play at Nice and Lyon respectively later Saturday.

Defending champions Paris Saint-Germain have just five points from their opening four games and visit bitter rivals Marseille on Sunday.

title: Michigan football's 5-star edge looks ready to go vs UTEP
description: While U-M has five-star edge Carter Meadows dressed for the first time in his career, it's now missing a starting offensive lineman.
fullText:
For the first time in his career, Michigan football five-star edge Carter Meadows is dressed on game day.

The freshman who was out the first two weeks of the season was warming up with the team prior to the game and after coach Kyle Whittingham said it looked like he'd "be good to go" in Week 3 against UTEP, he appears in position to take his first snaps with the Wolverines.

The Wolverines, however, are down a starting offensive lineman. Andrew Sprague, who's been a mainstay at right tackle, is not in uniform and will not play in Week 3, a program spokesman confirmed to the Detroit Free Press. Sprague has played all 115 offensive snaps for the Wolverines this season and started 12 of 13 games in 2025.

Sprague was one of two offensive linemen who early in fall camp had emerged as a starter, when offensive line coach Jim Harding said the right tackle spot was "his to lose." While U-M's offensive line has not had a great start to the year, Sprague has been one of the more consistent pieces.

In other offensive line news, Evan Link, who started at left guard and dressed last week but did not play (which Whittingham later said was health related) is once again dressed and going through warmups. When U-M lined up in its offensive line vs. defensive line warmups, Link was taking reps at left tackle while Blake Frazier (who usually starts there) had flipped to the right side.

FOLLOW ALONG: Michigan football vs UTEP live updates, Week 3 game score, highlights

Nathan Efobi was at left guard, Jake Guarnera at center and Brady Norton at right guard while Andrew Babalola, the five-star from the class of 2025, is still out, as expected.

Elsewhere, the Wolverines have swapped health in the tight end room.

Hogan Hansen, who missed the first two weeks of the season, is dressed for the first time this season, but Deakon Tonielli is not suited up for undisclosed reasons. The senior caught eight passes for 72 yards in 2025, but has not seen a snap on offense this season, playing 10 snaps in each of the first two games, all on special teams.

Wide receiver Jamar Browder is also not dressed. He has not taken a snap for U-M this season.

title: FINAL: Kansas State 31, Tulane 20
description: Avery Johnson and Jaron Tibbs eviscerated the Tulane defense in Kansas State’s win.
fullText:
A first-half struggle turned into second-half dominance as Kansas State rode a career day by Jaron Tibbs and the best performance of the year by Avery Johnson to roll to a 31-20 victory over the Tulane Green Wave on Saturday at Bill Snyder Family Stadium in Manhattan.

Johnson accounted for 379 yards of offense between his arm and legs, and Tibbs set career highs in both catches and yards. The Wildcat defense finally bent, giving up two touchdowns, but they forced Tulane (1-2) to eat a lot of clock in the process.

K-State (3-0) won the toss as well as the opening drive, forcing a 3-and-out. But the offense stalled, and the Cats had to punt. On Tulane's second drive, the Wildcat defense finally had a breakdown, giving up a 41-yard pass from Kadin Semonza to Oliver Mitchell as well as a pair big runs before Semonza scored on a nine-yard run. It was the first touchdown surrendered on the season by the Wildcat defense.

Another fruitless drive by the Cats was followed by a huge tackle for loss by Gabe Powers on a blown running play which led to a punt giving K-State decent field position. A 33-yard connection between Johnson and Tibbs and an 11-yard jet sweep by Brandon White got the Cats down to the four-yard line, but on the next three plays the Cats lost a yard. Luis Rodriguez came on to kick a 23-yarder to get K-State on the board at 7-3.

After two 10+ yard runs, an Elijah Hill sack led to a Tulane punt. Johnson picked up two first downs with his legs, then completed two big passes to Tibbs and Will Anciaux to get down to the Tulane two-yard line. Two plays later, Jay Harris bulled in to give the Cats a 10-7 lead.

Tulane went 3-and-out, and after an incompletion Johnson broke free down the sideline for 66 yards, then scored from seven yards out. Tulane ran the two-minute drill well until Jayden Bryant plowed Semonza for a loss of 13 on a third-down sack, and Tulane had to settle for a 58-yard field goal attempt by Cooper Helmke — which would have been good from 70. The Cats killed the final 17 seconds and took a 17-10 lead into the locker room.

After the break, K-State methodically moved downfield, eating up over eight minutes. The biggest play was a 27-yard completion to Anciaux, and Harris capped things with a one-yard run. Tulane responded, aided by a pair of concurrent penalties which erased a 21-yard gain by DJ Dugar; a late hit by Mekhi Mason resulted in 15 yards instead. Tulane got down the the 24, but a 1-yard stop, a 5-yard loss, and a 7-yard sack pushed them back to the 35 and a 4th-and-21. Helmke pounded a 53-yarder to bring the score to 24-13.

As the third quarter ended, on 4th-and-inches at theWildcats' own 34, Collin Klein opted to punt and rely on the defense. It paid off with a 3-and-out, and a 14-yard catch by Tibbs plus a 25-yard run by Johnson got K-State into the red zone. Johnson ran it in from 12 yards out a couple of plays later for a 31-13 advantage.

Tulane got a 22-yard gain on a pass play, then three plays later faced 3rd-and-19 but were bailed out by a pass interference call on Kaleb Patterson when Semonza was nearly sacked by Koy Beasley. Inside the 30, Bryant got his second sack of the day, but then on 3rd-and-17 Semonza found Maurice Turner for a 25-yard score to get within 31-20.

Tulane tried an onside kick, but K-State recovered, and after a first-down pass to Garrett Oakley after Tulane had exhausted their final time out, Johnson knelt the clock out for the win.

Johnson was fantastic today after a couple of shaky starts to begin the season. He was 21-28 for 227 yards although with no touchdown passes, and had a career-high 152 yards on 12 carries with two scores. The rest of the team only accounted for 49 yards on the ground, although with two touchdowns courtesy of Jay Harris.

Tibbs set career highs in both receptions (9) and yards (114). The tight ends were busy as well, with 4 catches for 27 yards for Oakley, 3 for 59 for Anciaux, and 3 for 23 for Linkin Cure.

K-State outgained Tulane 428-260, 201-95 on the ground and 227-165 in the air. Both teams were penalized five times, although K-State lost 34 more yards as a result than the Green Wave. There were no turnovers, and K-State led time of possession 33:41-26:19. The biggest eye popper on the stat sheet: Johnson was not sacked, while the Cats got to Semonza six times, and had 12 tackles for loss for a total of 64 yards.

Johnson was able to get yards himself, but the rest of the stable struggled today. Tulane was well-prepared, and the Cats are going to have to address that issue in conference play or things could get hairy.

They didn't get gashed horribly — in fact, on paper it looked like another great performance. But Tulane was able to get decent chunks and used the run game to move the chains often, and subtracting sack yardage like sane people do makes the numbers look a lot worse.

Semonza's numbers through the air today will be the cause of nightmares… for him.

Tibbs was mostly the invisible man in K-State's opening pair of games, but he was Johnson's favorite today. He had career highs in both receptions and yards, and while he didn't find the end zone himself he had a big part in every Wildcat touchdown today.

Cure caught 3 balls on three targets, presented a threat in the run game although he had no carries, and was on the field for most of the game. I think we can stop clutching our pearls.

Johnson had his best game of the year, but when you have a career day we're giving you the nod here. So Jaron Tibbs gets the nod this week. On defense, Will Gregory was once again great — three tackles for loss and half a sack — but we'll spread the love around and give it to Jayden Bryant and his two sacks and two TFLs this week.

The Cincinnati Bearcats come to Manhattan to open conference play in an evening game on ESPN2.

title: Gophers-Akron player ratings: Javon Tracy flashes, offense slow to get going
description: Minnesota's offense found a way to put up points on Saturday.
fullText:
The Gophers took care of business in Week 3 with a 41-7 win over Akron, but the scoreboard doesn't explain the whole story. Darius Taylor being ruled out pregame was an obstacle; a sluggish offensive start prevented Minnesota from hitting its stride until the fourth quarter.

It appears that Harbaugh didn't have much of an interest in even trying to run the ball in the first half without Taylor. The Gophers' running backs had seven rushing attempts compared to 23 pass attempts from Lindsey. An explosion in the fourth quarter did a lot of heavy lifting for three quarters of underwhelming offensive football. Play-calling in the red zone continues to look concerning for the offense.

The Gophers' defense began to showcase many of the playmakers we thought they had before the season. They had two sacks and one turnover in the first-half, but Akron still had some success moving the football. Ultimately, it was an improvement from Week 2, but there's still a long way to go before Big Ten play.

Lindsey's streak of 213 completions without an interception came to an end on Saturday, but he got better as the game went on. He finished 17 of 31 for 2041 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. His touchdown throw to Jalen Smith might've been his best of the game.

Big-time throw and catch from Drake Lindsey to Jalen Smith for his first touchdown of the season.

Cannot place a ball much better. pic.twitter.com/woFaUgS1lb

The Gophers had almost zero success running the football for three quarters. They finished the first-half with 1.3 yards per carry as a team. TJ Thomas and A.J. Turner found their groove as the game went on, making the decision to completely abandon the run in the first-half even more confusing. There's plenty to build off with 193 yards on the ground against Akron, but still a lot of questions ahead of Big Ten play.

Tracy should've had another punt return for a touchdown, but he did finish with 171 all-purpose yards. He's clearly this team's most consistent offensive weapon in years, and he helped hide some concerning long-term issues for the offense.

Jennings continues to look like Minnesota's No. 2 receiver, and he finished with five catches for 72 yards and one touchdown. He has seemingly usurped Jalen Smith in the order of Lindsey's favorite targets, which gives the Gophers another legit pass-catcher.

Maverick Baranowski, Emmanuel Karmo and Matt Kingsbury were projected to be Minnesota's rotation at inside linebacker before the season, but Gerlach has made his presence felt through three weeks. He had a strip sack last week that led to a touchdown. He forced a fumble and recovered another against Akron. He has come back from a season-ending injury last year stronger than ever, and he's one of the most important players on Minnesota's defense.

Despite Greg Johnson continuing to get hype as a future first-round pick, Minnesota's offensive line, and specifically run blocking, has been underwhelming. Center Ashton Beers missed a little bit of Saturday's game, and they began to find their groove late in the fourth quarter.

It's hard to poke too many holes in a 41-0 win, but the Gophers' performance doesn't feel like it instills that much confidence heading into a hostile environment next week at Washington. The Gophers had a lot of problems exposed last week against Mississippi State, and their performance makes it feel like they haven't solved many of them.

We are in the age of big media consolidation and content networks. But even with the proliferation of AI, nothing can beat the quality and inherent knowledge of local sports journalism. Our writing room consists of a Wildcat, a Gopher, and even a Mustang. We know the Minnesota towns and the great names that played on its diamonds, courts, fields or rinks. We would appreciate your readership and support!

title: Vikings Deliver Harsh Reality Check On Kyler Murray’s Status After Scary Concussion Hit
description: Kyler Murray wanted to secure his place as the undisputed leader of the Minnesota Vikings, but a violent helmet collision abruptly halted his debut. Now that the quarterback has been sidelined by league concussion protocols, his team is searching for stability in the position as medical evaluations continue. Carson Wentz steps in under center. J.J.
fullText:
Kyler Murray wanted to secure his place as the undisputed leader of the Minnesota Vikings, but a violent helmet collision abruptly halted his debut. Now that the quarterback has been sidelined by league concussion protocols, his team is searching for stability in the position as medical evaluations continue.

Carson Wentz steps in under center. J.J. McCarthy settles behind him on the depth chart, but the situation has increased pressure on the Vikings early in the season.

Murray played only 11 snaps against the Green Bay Packers before a hard tackle forced him out of his Minnesota debut. The Vikings fell behind 22-10, but Carson Wentz took over to help finish a 39-22 comeback win with three touchdown passes.

Coach Kevin O'Connell later gave an update on Murray's recovery. "Kyler showed a lot of progress. He's doing well, felt good this week working through it, but he will be out Sunday. Fully anticipate him clearing the protocol early next week with the progress that he's made," O'Connell said in the team video.

He also confirmed the immediate depth-chart change: "Carson will start and JJ will be the backup. Carson had a really good week of work coming off of his performance last week and I know he's ready to go."

That decision removed Murray from the Vikings' Week 2 game against the Chicago Bears, shifting McCarthy into the backup role. McCarthy entered the season behind Murray alongside Wentz, having competed for a larger place in the quarterback plan. The former first-round pick now faces an extended wait for another opening.

Wentz has a chance to protect Minnesota's early lead in the quarterback room. His relief performance gave the Vikings a short-term answer, but Chicago's defense will test him.

With Kyler Murray sidelined, the Vikings turned to Carson Wentz rather than handing the reins to McCarthy which was a telling sign of where the coaching staff's trust currently sits.

O'Connell also explained Minnesota's quarterback balance. "We want him to be able to have the ability to impact the game with his legs… a situation like that where there's a vice tackle opportunity short of the sticks, those are the situations where I love that he went down. But he plays with such explosive explosiveness, he was trying to go down feet first, and just the momentum and he ended up kind of going sideways down to his left side."

The Vikings' earlier status report left open Murray's chance to clear the protocol but now their hopes of having their QB1 in Week 2 is all but quashed. Minnesota can reassess after Murray returns, but Wentz's 39-22 comeback changed the pressure.

title: Eagles vs. Titans preview: Get to know Philadelphia’s Week 2 opponent
description: A closer look at Cam Ward, Jeffery Simmons and the Titans before Philadelphia travels to Nashville for its first road game
fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles will play their first road game of the season Sunday when they visit a Tennessee Titans team attempting to establish a new identity. Tennessee lost its opener to the New York Jets, 23-10, and finished with only 195 yards of offense. Quarterback Cam Ward struggled to create explosive plays in his first regular-season game under offensive coordinator Brian Daboll, while a rebuilt defense surrendered 367 yards.

The Titans are seven-point home underdogs, but their defensive front, return game, and mobile quarterback give Philadelphia several legitimate concerns.

Here is what Eagles fans should know about Tennessee entering Week 2.

Tennessee was held to 10 points while losing its home opener to the Jets.

The Titans gained 68 rushing yards and 127 net passing yards. They converted four of 12 third downs and committed one turnover.

Tennessee's defense allowed 215 passing yards and 152 rushing yards. The Jets converted only two of 12 third downs but still controlled enough of the game to leave Nashville with a 13-point victory.

Saleh is in his first season as Tennessee's head coach after previously leading the Jets and serving as San Francisco's defensive coordinator.

His defenses are traditionally built around a disruptive four-man front, fast linebackers, and zone coverage. Tennessee hired former Jacksonville head coach Gus Bradley as defensive coordinator, giving Saleh another experienced voice with a similar foundational philosophy.

Brian Daboll was hired to coordinate the offense and oversee Ward's development.

Ward completed 19 of 32 passes for 140 yards and one touchdown in Week 1. He was sacked three times and rushed four times for 21 yards. The production was modest, but Ward's talent remains evident. He can make throws from different platforms, attack tight windows, and create after the original play breaks down.

Vic Fangio identified Ward's arm strength and mobility as two of his defining traits. That combination gives Philadelphia a second consecutive test against an athletic quarterback after Jayden Daniels repeatedly escaped pressure in Week 1.

The Eagles must pressure Ward without creating open scrambling lanes.

Daboll wants to develop a balanced offense that uses Ward's mobility, play-action, and quick passing concepts. The opener never developed that rhythm. The Titans averaged 3.4 yards per rushing attempt and did not create enough manageable third downs. Ward frequently operated in obvious passing situations, allowing the Jets to attack Tennessee's protection.

Establishing the running game would make Daboll's entire call sheet available. Philadelphia allowed Washington to possess the ball for 33 minutes, 20 seconds and must avoid allowing Tennessee to build a similar advantage.

Calvin Ridley remains Tennessee's most accomplished receiver, though he wasn't targeted in Week 1 despite running routes on most of Ward's dropbacks. That disconnect should make getting him involved an obvious priority. First-round rookie Carnell Tate gives Tennessee another polished route runner with size and ball skills. The Titans selected Tate with the fourth overall pick to grow alongside Ward.

Tight end Gunnar Helm is a reliable short-area target who can help Ward when Philadelphia's pass rush forces him to deliver the ball quickly.

Tennessee also has young talent in the backfield. Regardless of how the carries are distributed, the Titans need greater efficiency after managing only 68 rushing yards against New York.

The Titans' protection allowed three sacks in Week 1 and struggled to create consistent displacement in the running game.

Philadelphia will not have Jonathan Greenard, but Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith Jr., Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa should still have opportunities to affect Ward.

Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis can make the matchup uncomfortable from the interior. Carter and Cooper DeJean received no final injury designations, while Davis is coming off a seven-tackle performance.

The challenge is maintaining rush discipline. Pressure will mean little if the Eagles allow Ward to escape the pocket and attack open space.

Simmons remains the player Philadelphia must identify before every snap.

The three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle can align over either guard, attack the center, or move outside in passing situations. His strength, first-step quickness, and ability to split double teams create problems against any offensive line.

His matchup becomes more significant with Landon Dickerson on injured reserve. Philadelphia could turn to Fred Johnson, Drew Kendall or Willie Lampkin at left guard.

Simmons will be tasked with performing after stating that Tennessee must contain Hurts and "make him be a quarterback." The comment drew attention because Hurts threw for 380 yards and three touchdowns while adding a rushing score during Philadelphia's 35-10 victory over Tennessee in 2022.

Franklin-Myers signed a three-year, $63 million contract to form an imposing interior combination with Simmons.

His Tennessee debut was quiet. Franklin-Myers recorded three tackles and one pressure against the Jets, but his power and versatility could trouble Philadelphia's reshuffled line.

The Eagles cannot direct all their protection help toward Simmons and assume the remainder of Tennessee's front will remain quiet.

Tennessee added Jermaine Johnson II to strengthen its pass rush. Johnson recorded one pressure in Week 1 but has the explosiveness to challenge tackles around the corner.

Rookie Femi Oladejo also showed promising flashes during training camp and the opener. His motor and developing power could earn him additional snaps against Philadelphia.

The Titans recorded nine total pressures in Week 1. They will need considerably more disruption to prevent Hurts from attacking their secondary.

Hill recorded 16 tackles in his NFL debut, the most by a linebacker in a first-game league record.

The rookie's speed, range, and physicality make him a central figure against Saquon Barkley and Hurts. Tennessee must account for Barkley between the tackles while preventing Hurts from turning broken plays into first downs.

Cedric Gray has cleared concussion protocol, giving the Titans another young linebacker who can contribute beside Hill.

The secondary remains one of Tennessee's greatest questions after extensive offseason changes.

Saleh and Bradley will attempt to protect the group with zone coverage, disciplined eyes, and pressure from the front. That approach becomes difficult if Simmons and the edge rushers cannot make Hurts uncomfortable.

DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon give Philadelphia several favorable matchups. Hollywood Brown could also receive his first offensive snaps after practicing fully on Friday.

Dike earned first-team All-Pro honors as a rookie and can change field position on punts or kickoffs.

Eagles special-teams coordinator Michael Clay specifically identified Dike as a major concern. Philadelphia's coverage players reached Washington's returners in Week 1 but allowed additional yardage by stopping their feet at contact.

The Eagles cannot repeat those tackling mistakes against one of the NFL's most dangerous return specialists.

The defensive front is the Titans' clearest strength.

Simmons is an elite interior defender, Franklin-Myers has produced across multiple schemes, and Johnson gives Tennessee another talented edge rusher. That group will attack an Eagles line playing without Dickerson.

If Tennessee can disrupt Hurts without blitzing, it can devote additional defenders to Barkley, Smith, Goedert and Philadelphia's other receiving threats.

The offense did not produce enough or generate enough explosive plays in Week 1.

Tennessee ranked 31st in total offense, 30th in rushing and 29th in net passing after its opener. Ward averaged 4.4 yards per attempt, while the Titans produced 10 points. The small sample needs perspective, but Philadelphia has a chance to force Ward into another inefficient game by winning early downs and making Tennessee operate in obvious passing situations.

The Titans enter the game relatively healthy. Gray cleared concussion protocol, strengthening the linebacker rotation.

Philadelphia ruled out Greenard because of a pectoral injury. Safety Andrew Mukuba is questionable with a knee injury.

Carter, DeJean, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore received no game-status designation and are available.

Philadelphia and Tennessee last met on Dec. 4, 2022, when the Eagles earned a 35-10 victory at Lincoln Financial Field.

Hurts completed 29 of 39 passes for 380 yards and three touchdowns. He also rushed for a score. A.J. Brown caught eight passes for 119 yards and two touchdowns against his former team.

The Eagles lead the all-time series 8-5, but Tennessee won three of the previous four meetings before Philadelphia's dominant 2022 performance.

Tennessee is rebuilding around Ward, Saleh and a collection of young players, but the Titans possess enough defensive talent to make Philadelphia work. The Eagles must protect their reshuffled interior, contain Ward without sacrificing rush-lane discipline, and prevent Dike from shifting field position.

If Philadelphia stays ahead of the chains and forces Tennessee to sustain long scoring drives, its overall talent should produce an efficient 2-0 start. The clearest path to an upset begins with Simmons disrupting the pocket and Ward creating explosive plays after escaping it.

title: Game Discussion: Milwaukee Brewers (96-58) @ Baltimore Orioles (75-79)
description: Robert Gasser, Trevor Rogers square off in battle of the lefties
fullText:
After scraping out a victory in last night's series opener against the Orioles, the Brewers are one game closer to securing the best record in baseball — and the number one seed heading into the playoffs.

On the mound to try to secure a series win for Milwaukee is lefty Robert Gasser, who has become the Brewers' third-most-reliable starter behind Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson. Gasser is a former top prospect who, almost immediately after reaching the majors in 2024, tore his UCL. This season is his first full season back from that injury, and he's been pretty good, all things considered. Gasser has a 4.30 ERA and a 1.27 WHIP through 19 appearances (18 starts), although he's pitched better than those numbers suggest for stretches.

Pitching for the Orioles is Trevor (not Taylor, nor Tyler) Rogers. For the most part, Rogers has been for Baltimore what Gasser is to the Brewers: a dependable, if not spectacular, lefty who will at least keep his team in the game. He comes into today's game with a 4.22 ERA and a 1.22 WHIP in 28 starts.

Although it's Saturday, Brewers manager Pat Murphy is rolling out a lineup that would fit right in on a Sunday. Jake Bauers, Brice Turang, Sal Frelick, and Christian Yelich will all get the day off after yesterday's extra-inning thriller.

Jackson Chourio, the Brewers' hottest hitter right now, leads off, followed by Garrett Mitchell and William Contreras, who will serve as the designated hitter today. The middle of the order consists of Andrew Vaughn, Joey Ortiz, and catcher Gary Sánchez. Rounding out the lineup are Cooper Pratt, Luis Lara, and David Hamilton, who will play second base in Turang's absence.

As usual, today's game will be broadcast on Brewers.TV, WTMJ 620, and the Brewers Radio Network. First pitch is set for 3:05 p.m.

title: Wrexham's boost & Alexander in ideal place - Aaron McLean's EFL takeaways
description: BBC Final Score pundit Aaron McLean looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including Wrexham, QPR and Bradford City.
fullText:
Former Peterborough United and Hull City striker - and Final Score pundit - Aaron McLean gives his five takeaways following Saturday's action in the Championship, League One and League Two.

Wrexham ended Southampton's five-match unbeaten run by winning 2-1 to claim their first home win of the season. Expectations remain high in north Wales, such is the public profile of the club and the investment into the squad but they have been an inconsistent prospect so far this campaign.

McLean: "Do I think Wrexham are a candidate for automatic promotion? Probably not, but that win against Southampton will give them huge confidence.

"That was only their second win of the season and they have probably come under pressure for the first time. Last season they were outstanding and, personally I think overachieved and the level of expectation has risen as a result but the team has not quite lived up to it.

"To beat Southampton, as one of the in-form teams in the division, will do them and Phil Parkinson no end of good.

"They need to be more clinical. You look at West Ham – 22 goals; Middlesbrough – 16 goals. You look at the top end of the pitch and they have the players who can find ways to kill games off.

"Wrexham have drawn four games because they have not been able to kill games off but, if they are in the shake-up, I would not bet against their owners in January saying, 'right, let's go and get the missing piece of the puzzle'."

Wrexham earn last-gasp victory over Southampton

Given Preston's predicament towards the foot of the Championship, QPR may well feel their 2-2 draw was two points dropped but they fought back from 2-0 down and Dennis Cirkin's red card in the 15th minute to claim a draw at Loftus Road. Julien Stephan's R's are fifth in the Championship table and remain firmly in the promotion mix.

McLean: "I have been so impressed with QPR. I think they have been outstanding and they can genuinely stay around the play-off places.

"Glen Kamara in the middle of the park is an outstanding player who I think could play in the Premier League. Their recruitment has been first class.

"With the squad they have got, I really like the look of them this season. For a few years they have probably spent money in the wrong places but they have addressed that and can look forward to having a really competitive season.

"Julien Stephan has done a hugely impressive job – the 7-1 defeat to Coventry [at the start of last season] has been the making of them – and I am really looking forward to seeing them over the rest of the season."

QPR score last-minute equaliser against Preston

Bradford City's 58-year wait for a win over Luton Town has enabled them to usurp Sheffield Wednesday at the top of League One. The Bantams have only scored seven goals in seven games but have conceded just four - the joint-best defensive record in the EFL. Predictably, given his history at Deepdale as a player, Graham Alexander has been linked with the vacancy at Preston North End.

McLean: "Bradford are a massive club, you only have to listen to the noise they make at Valley Parade and the support they get and Graham Alexander is an outstanding manager who is at the right club for him to continue progressing.

"This season, their bouncebackability has stood out. They won their first two games, then after back-to-back defeats you are looking at them and thinking, 'oh was it just a good start' but then they go and win three in a row, so even in adversity they can bounce back and respond in the right way.

"Is their lack of goals sustainable for a promotion challenge? No, probably not but, at the moment, it hasn't needed to be because they have been so good defensively and so hard to beat.

"And that's from front to back and when they do get their noses in front, they know how to see games out.

"I expect their conversion rate to improve and Bobby Pointon is a fantastic young striker who I have tipped to be one of the best strikers in the division over the next few seasons."

Bromley ended Huddersfield Town's unbeaten start to the season with a 2-1 victory at the Copperjax Community Stadium - their first since the opening day of the 2026-27 season. It has been a challenging first few weeks for the club in the third tier for the first time in their history, losing three games in a row and conceding 14 goals in the process but Andy Woodman's squad have shown their resilience and quality to come through that period.

McLean: "For Bromley, it is sometimes easy to lose sight of where they have come from, how quickly they have got here, and the jump that exists between League Two and the top end of League One. It is really, really tough for newly-promoted teams and it is going to take time to adapt.

"To come out winners against Huddersfield who were the form team in the division will do them the world of good.

"It shows they have the character and the belief in the dressing room that even on the back of a run of defeats they can go again, and compete and get positive results against teams of the size of Huddersfield.

"Andy Woodman will be absolutely delighted. For a club of Bromley's size and where they have been, consolidation in League One will surely be the goal this season and these three points will go a long way to helping achieve that."

Since dropping down to League Two four years ago, Gillingham have never finished higher than 12th, a poor return for a club of their size and reputation. But their eye-catching 3-0 win over Bristol Rovers means they are now the form side in the division with three wins and three draws over their past six and have moved up to fourth with signs pointing towards something stirring within Gareth Ainsworth's squad.

McLean: "I spoke to Gareth Ainsworth in the summer and he admitted he got it wrong last season. They perhaps overachieved a bit at the start and that created a false impression of where they were as a squad.

"Gareth has ripped up the script a bit and they have looked really really positive and are playing their way into form.

"He is huge on the psychological aspect of management and players 'emptying the tank' and to play for Gareth Ainsworth you have to buy into that.

"When you look at their performances and the way they are achieving these results it looks like another squad of players who have bought into his ideas.

"You look at his Wycombe sides, you don't have to be the biggest club in the division as long as everyone is pulling in the right direction then you can be successful."

Aaron McLean was speaking to BBC Sport England's James Piercy

title: The Real Reason Ole Miss Remained Skeptical Of Sam Leavitt’s Injury Status All Week
description: Sam Leavitt is set to start at quarterback for LSU Tigers against No. 8 Ole Miss. fullText:
Sam Leavitt is set to start at quarterback for LSU Tigers against No. 8 Ole Miss. His status changed quickly this week, going from doubtful to questionable before he was removed from the injury report entirely.

The news comes as Lane Kiffin makes his first return to Oxford since taking over at LSU. With Leavitt cleared, the Tigers will have their starting quarterback for the SEC opener.

Sam Leavitt was removed from the SEC injury report Friday night, clearing the way for him to face No. 8 Ole Miss. The quarterback was first listed as doubtful on Wednesday before being upgraded to questionable Thursday after taking part in LSU's walkthrough.

Leavitt did not practice Wednesday, and reports during the week said he was dealing with soreness in his throwing shoulder. LSU did not publicly list a specific injury on its official report.

The Arizona State transfer has started both of LSU's games this season. He has completed 41 of 66 passes for 574 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also rushed 23 times for 135 yards and five touchdowns.

Leavitt's latest performance came in LSU's 45-14 win over Louisiana Tech. He completed 25 of 38 passes for 344 yards and one touchdown while scoring three rushing touchdowns. He also threw three interceptions in the game.

Arizona State transfer Sam Leavitt made his LSU debut against Clemson in the season opener after joining Lane Kiffin's offense. His return to the field now gives LSU another key piece heading into its first SEC game of the season.

Yahoo Sports then shared the update on X with the caption, "Sam Leavitt is good to go for tomorrow's showdown with No. 8 Ole Miss [

The SEC requires teams to release an injury report every Wednesday, with updates on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays. Leavitt's removal from the report means LSU will have its regular starting quarterback available for the game.

LSU enters the matchup 2-0 and ranked No. 7, while Ole Miss is also 2-0 and ranked No. 8. The game is scheduled for Saturday at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium.

Lane Kiffin will return to Ole Miss as LSU's head coach after leaving the Rebels following the 2025 season. He spent six seasons at Ole Miss and went 55-19. His return to Oxford comes in LSU's SEC opener against the program he led for six seasons.

Leavitt is expected to play a central role in LSU's offense this season. Kiffin's return has also brought a response from Ole Miss fans. Extra security has been planned around the stadium and campus, with state and local law enforcement adding personnel for the game.

Lane Kiffin's daughter Landry Kiffin also addressed inappropriate comments directed at her on social media during the buildup to the game, saying she should not be part of the dispute surrounding her father's return. She said, "I think that turning a girl into the punchline of a sexual joke because you're upset at somebody she's related to should not be okay. I understand emotions are high this week and people are upset, but I'm my own person."

Several Ole Miss players will be important to Kiffin in his return. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has 561 passing yards, five touchdowns and one interception through two games. Running back Kewan Lacy has 148 rushing yards and three touchdowns, while wide receiver Deuce Alexander has 235 receiving yards and two touchdowns.

LSU also has players with connections to Ole Miss. Edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen transferred from Ole Miss to LSU and has five sacks this season. Linebacker TJ Dottery has been one of LSU's leading tacklers, while tight end Trey'Dez Green is one of the Tigers' main receiving options.

With Leavitt available and both teams entering undefeated, LSU and Ole Miss will meet in one of the SEC's most anticipated early-season matchups.

title: Bills’ Heartfelt Gesture Makes Highmark Stadium Debut Unforgettable for Buffalo

The stadium finally welcomed the fans and the organization didn’t forget to make it special […] The post Bills’ Heartfelt Gesture Makes Highmark Stadium Debut Unforgettable for Buffalo appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
For over fifty years, Buffalo Bills' football thrived in the raw, ice-bound atmosphere of the original Highmark Stadium. Due to the necessity of modern facilities Bills' went through a transition and now they have a $2.1 billion dollar worth stadium.

The stadium finally welcomed the fans and the organization didn't forget to make it special for the fans. Bills made sure the fans feel inclusive and they had a clear message to do that.

Buffalo Bills new Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York, hosted its official regular-season debut on Thursday, September 17, 2026, when the Buffalo Bills faced the Detroit Lions on Thursday Night Football.

The opening night event was designed as a major regional celebration, featuring a halftime concert by OneRepublic, a dual-anthem performance featuring "O Canada" alongside the U.S. national anthem to honor the region's strong Canadian fanbase, and an ceremonial ownership celebration before kickoff.

To mark the historic opening, the organization distributed custom physical replica keys to every fan entering the gates as a keepsake. It came with a lamented card which had a message for all the fans. "Today we open a new chapter of Buffalo Bills history. Highmark stadium is the celebration of a city and a team built by generations of loyalty, resilience and pride. It stands on the communities unwavering support and dedication to the Buffalo Bills. A fanbase whose passion extends beyond Western New York and starts right here at Highmark stadium," the card read.

"This stadium is yours Buffalo. Welcome Home," the card read at the end. Within hours of the turnstiles opening, photos of the collectible keys flooded social media platforms, with several turning up on secondary market sites like eBay as fans and collectors scrambled to buy a piece of opening-night history.

In the inauguration of the new stadium, Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions put on a high-scoring game in which the Bills took the victory.

Buffalo Bills opened the game with an offensive explosion. The offense was practically unstoppable through the first two quarters, racking up 299 total yards before halftime and building a commanding 27-10 lead at the break. Though the Lions mounted several pushbacks in the second half behind Jared Goff, Bills held firm to seal a 10-point victory and move to 2-0 on the season.

Bills quarterback Josh Allen delivered a dominant performance, single-handedly accounting for five touchdowns. He finished the night with 248 passing yards and 69 rushing yards, becoming the first player in NFL history with 5+ passing touchdowns and 3+ rushing touchdowns through the first two games of a season.

Running back James Cook spearheaded the ground game, churning out 101 rushing yards on 11 carries, aided by explosive back-to-back 20+ yard gains in the second quarter. Defensive end Greg Rousseau set the tone early for Buffalo's defense, recording 2.0 sacks in the first 13 minutes of play. His performance made him only the second Bills player in franchise history alongside Hall of Famer Bruce Smith in 1996 to record multiple sacks in each of the first two games of a season.

title: Burrillville enjoying first sight of Friday night lights
description: A project that was once delayed because of opposition is now complete and fans turned out for the Broncos' Friday night game vs. West Warwick.
fullText:
BURRILLVILLE – Up until about two weeks ago, Burrillville had not experienced a Friday-night high school football game under stadium lighting.

It may seem like a minor accomplishment, but there's a spark in the eyes of fans who watched their home varsity Broncos beat West Warwick 43-19 on Sept. 18 at the newly constructed Thomas E. Gledhill Memorial Field in Harrisville. They think it's electric. Something like this has never been experienced on home turf before.

"I wish I played on it," said Nate Njoes, a former right tackle and defensive lineman for Burrillville who graduated last year.

Oddly enough, turf was one of the sticking points in local opposition of the project to construct the field, as those against said use of the artificial grass and its required treatment would contaminate the local water supply. There were also concerns of injuries related to playing on turf.

The project was delayed after beginning in 2024 because of the pushback. Now, as fans pack the newly constructed field and bleachers, past lawsuits and legal challenges seem at the back of most minds.

"To see it completed and built is really cool," said Joshua Cookson, Burrillville High School Class of 2025. "We saw it in the process and to see the finish line is great. I just wish we got to experience this. I've never seen so many people here."

Even visiting fans are impressed.

"It's beautiful, and it's really nice to come here and play under the lights," said Chelsea Lubera of West Warwick. "I'm happy they got to add this. It makes the football experience better for Burrillville, but also for the teams who come to play them."

The town officially unveiled the new field on Aug. 26. Burrillville played its first contest there on Sept. 4, winning the Rhode Island Interscholastic League Injury Fund exhibition game against the East Greenwich Avengers. Word quickly spread around town about the new field's appeal.

"The atmosphere is incredible over here," said Kyle Maciel, a former linebacker for Burrillville who graduated in 2025. "Under the lights, man, this is what high school football is really all about."

Previous games were played on Saturdays on the grass on the smaller Alumni Field, just up the hill on the high school campus. They did not draw as much of a crowd, fans said. It can be difficult for students, families and residents to dedicate a precious weekend day to high school sports consistently. But football on Friday nights is a different story.

"It feels like we're a real school now," said one current student.

Burrillville will take on Portsmouth at the new field on Sept. 25.

This article originally appeared on The Providence Journal: Burrillville enjoying first sight of Friday night lights

title: Colin Kaepernick Fires Blunt Shot at NFL’s Current Quarterback Class
description: Colin Kaepernick wants another chance in the NFL after nearly a decade away from the field. The former quarterback says he continues training hard and believes he can keep up with today’s starters. He has not played an official game since Jan. 1, 2017. Kaepernick has maintained that the league blacklisted him after his national […] The post Colin Kaepernick Fires Blunt Shot at NFL’s Current Quarterback Class appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Colin Kaepernick wants another chance in the NFL after nearly a decade away from the field. The former quarterback says he continues training hard and believes he can keep up with today's starters.

He has not played an official game since Jan. 1, 2017. Kaepernick has maintained that the league blacklisted him after his national anthem protest, but he continues preparing for the day a franchise finally calls.

Kaepernick's last NFL appearance came after the 2016 season, when his national anthem protest made him one of the league's most debated players. He has not joined a roster since, but he says preparation remains within his control.

"I have to do everything that is in my control to make sure that I'm prepared. And I mean that whether that's training, whether that's making sure I'm making the right calls. I want to make sure that what I have control over, I'm showing up the best way possible there," Kaepernick said.

He added, "I still train five days a week. I'm up at 4:30 in the morning doing my training before I go about the rest of my day."

Kaepernick follows quarterback stat lines to see which teams might need help. He has not received an offer, but he continues training for one. His routine is designed to keep him ready for an NFL workout.

Kaepernick previously reached Super Bowl XLVII with the San Francisco 49ers. A team would have to evaluate his current ability after years away from NFL competition. Kaepernick's argument is that his daily work should earn that opportunity.

Kaepernick's explanation for his absence is connected to an ownership dispute. According to a report, he alleged that Robert Kraft and other owners coordinated against Macklemore after the rapper criticized Israel.

Kaepernick said the situation reminded him of his grievance: "The part that I hope people appreciate and take away in this moment is what [New England Patriots owner] Robert Kraft and what they're saying by denying Macklemore the opportunity to go out and perform with Ed Sheeran is they are willing to collude."

He added, "The [NFL owners] are openly colluding."

Those remain Kaepernick's allegations, not a court finding against Kraft or the 32 owners. His 2017 grievance with Eric Reid was settled confidentially in 2019, so no public liability finding followed. The dispute remains part of his explanation for his absence.

title: North Carolina leads Clemson 17-15 in fourth quarter in game delayed by lightning
description: Billy Edwards Jr. has thrown for 105 yards and a touchdown, Benjamin Hall has run for 126 yards and has a TD reception as North Carolina leads Clemson 17-15 with 8:11 remaining in the fourth quarter in a game delayed by lightning in the area.  When the game resumes the Tar Heels will have a second-and-goal at the Clemson 7.  Clemson freshman Tait Reynolds, making his first career start at quarterback, has completed 19 of 28 passes for 201 yards with one touchdown and one interception.
fullText:
CLEMSON, S.C. (AP) — Billy Edwards Jr. has thrown for 105 yards and a touchdown, Benjamin Hall has run for 126 yards and has a TD reception as North Carolina leads Clemson 17-15 with 8:11 remaining in the fourth quarter in a game delayed by lightning in the area.

When the game resumes the Tar Heels will have a second-and-goal at the Clemson 7.

Clemson freshman Tait Reynolds, making his first career start at quarterback, has completed 19 of 28 passes for 201 yards with one touchdown and one interception.

It is the ACC season opener for both teams.

It is the third straight Clemson game that has been delayed by weather. No rain has fallen at Memorial Stadium and the sun is shining.

North Carolina (2-0) jumped out to a 17-3 lead behind a 3-yard touchdown run by Demon June and a 15-yard TD pass from Edwards to Hall before Clemson's Nolan Hauser added a field goal to close out the first half.

Clemson (1-1) closed the gap to two in the third quarter when Hauser connected on his third field goal of the game and Reynolds found Christian Bentancur for a 27-yard strike for his first career TD pass. However, the 2-point conversion attempt that would have tied the game failed when Bryant Wesco's pass attempt to T.J. Moore failed off a trick play.

Reynolds had gone 24 drives (excluding kneeldowns) to open his career without leading a touchdown.

North Carolina came into the game after a tulmultous week in which defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, the son of head coach Bill Belichick, resigned from his position as the school concludes a probe into its football program. That made him the second high-profile resignation amid the probe, the other being general manager Michael Lombardi earlier this month.

Things have been rough in Clemson, too.

Dabo Swinney's job security has been questioned after the Tigers were thrashed 51-10 in their season opener by then-No. 11 LSU and managed only one touchdown against Georgia Southern in a 22-7 win last week.

Clemson: The Tigers head out West to face California on Friday night.

North Carolina: The Tar Heels have a bye next weekend before hosting No. 3 Notre Dame on Oct. 3.

title: Laporta takes aim at Atletico after Barca miss out on Julian Alvarez
description: The president has had his say.
fullText:
Barcelona president Joan Laporta has taken aim at Atletico Madrid and the way the club behaved during the summer transfer window.

The Catalans wanted to sign Julian Alvarez from Atletico but saw the Madrid side hit out on social media at Barca and then refuse to sanction a move to the Camp Nou.

Atletico were reportedly willing to sell Alvarez to Arsenal, but the Argentina star made it clear he only wanted Barca.

Here's what Laporta has had to say about the saga.

"They acted offended; they had no way to justify their attitude. We did what's usually done: there was club-to-club communication, and then I spoke personally with Gil Marín. He told me he wasn't coming because they had no alternative," he said.

"Then they reacted inappropriately. I don't know why, I can imagine, but I have no proof. We were hearing that they would sell him to every club except Barça. Then they dropped the pretense and said it openly.

"That is now in the past and we are very happy with the squad we have and the coach is very happy with the extraordinary work of Deco."

Barcelona ended up switching Raphinha to a No. 9 role after missing out on Alvarez and have seen the Brazilian play a starring role for Hansi Flick's side, scoring 11 times in all competitions already.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Has Perfect Response to Cowboys’ Viral Pens Meme
description: During the Dallas Cowboys’ 28-20 Week 1 loss to the New York Giants, head coach Brian Schottenheimer was spotted with three pens tucked underneath his visor during the game. The unusual sight quickly became a source of amusement for Cowboys fans, who flooded social media with memes about the coach’s pen collection, something Schottenheimer has […] The post Brian Schottenheimer Has Perfect Response to Cowboys’ Viral Pens Meme appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
During the Dallas Cowboys' 28-20 Week 1 loss to the New York Giants, head coach Brian Schottenheimer was spotted with three pens tucked underneath his visor during the game. The unusual sight quickly became a source of amusement for Cowboys fans, who flooded social media with memes about the coach's pen collection, something Schottenheimer has now addressed himself.

While most NFL coaches might keep a pen tucked behind an ear or clipped somewhere on their shirt collar, Schottenheimer appears to have taken the practice to an entirely different level. It is rarely just one pen with him.

Television broadcasts have repeatedly captured close-up shots of the Cowboys coach wearing three, four, or sometimes even more pens, carefully tucked into the headband of his visor and wedged beneath his headset strap.

Recently, an AI generated photo of Schottenheimer went viral on social media showing what appeared to be an almost unbelievable number of pens stuffed into the headband of his visor.

On Friday, Schottenheimer was asked about the viral image and the attention surrounding his collection of pens. While discussing the Cowboys' preparations for Week 2, the head coach made it clear that the pens are not something he considers a distraction, while explaining that the different pens help him quickly distinguish between different notes and situations during the game.

"I am gonna get one of those pens that has the multi-colors," Schottenheimer said. "The (meme) with the entire head covered, I thought that might be a little overdone."

Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has seen this meme. “I am gonna get one of those pens that has the multi-colors. The (meme) with the entire head covered, I thought that might be a little overdone.

“… There are different colors I use for different things based on we called… pic.twitter.com/mCIIGMsemV

— Jon Machota (@jonmachota) September 18, 2026

"There are different colors I use for different things based on we called this, that's one color. I want to get to this, that's a different color. The pens are not a distraction to me, but it sounds like they are to some."

There is plenty that needs to improve for Dallas heading into Week 2 and beyond. The Cowboys defense gave up 394 total yards against the Giants, with New York managing to score at least one touchdown in every quarter. Meanwhile, Dallas' offense struggled to generate consistent production, finishing with only 244 total yards.

Schottenheimer is currently in his second season as the Cowboys' head coach after being promoted to the position in January 2025. He previously spent two seasons serving as Dallas' offensive coordinator before taking over as the team's head coach.

In his first season leading the Cowboys in 2025, Schottenheimer guided the team to a 7-9-1 record, but Dallas ultimately failed to qualify for the postseason.

title: We Now Know What Caused Travis Kelce’s Heated Off-Camera Feud Before Broncos Blowout
description: Travis Kelce became angry during warmups after Denver punters repeatedly disrupted Kansas City’s offensive drills in Week 1. ESPN’s Steve Coughlin said Kelce was frustrated by stray footballs interrupting Patrick Mahomes and the offense. Kelce eventually caught one of the loose punts and threw it into the stands. Travis Kelce unleashes pregame fury on Broncos […] The post We Now Know What Caused Travis Kelce’s Heated Off-Camera Feud Before Broncos Blowout appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Travis Kelce became angry during warmups after Denver punters repeatedly disrupted Kansas City's offensive drills in Week 1. ESPN's Steve Coughlin said Kelce was frustrated by stray footballs interrupting Patrick Mahomes and the offense.

Kelce eventually caught one of the loose punts and threw it into the stands.

The incident happened as Mahomes, Kelce and the Chiefs offense ran routes near midfield before facing Denver. Broncos punters were also working in the area, and their kicks repeatedly crossed the path of Kansas City's drills. Coughlin described the moment on the Stanford Steve podcast.

"Travis' eyes lit up and he sees the ball – it's a Broncos ball – and it goes over towards the Broncos' sideline," Coughlin recalled. "He catches his route, runs over to the ball, takes the Broncos ball and punts it almost to the second deck. Good punter, up to the deck."

Van Pelt asked, "Into the stands?" Coughlin replied, "Yeah, and now he's like looking for another one. Sure enough, he goes back, gives the ball up, goes back, runs his route and he's just steaming. You can see it. Here comes another one. So, now the Broncos ball boy is running over because he saw Travis do it again. Travis is like nope. He beats him to the ball, takes the Broncos ball and chucks it up in the stands. I'm like 'All right, we're back here! The Chiefs are in it.'"

"I didn't know that happened," Van Pelt added.

Coughlin's account places the dispute away from game action. It was a pregame practice-space conflict, not a reported penalty or league discipline. The preparation turned confrontational before kickoff.

Kelce's exchange recalled his 2024 AFC Championship confrontation with Ravens kicker Justin Tucker.

Tucker had set up near the goal line, and CBS reported that Mahomes tossed aside his kicking tee before Kelce kicked Tucker's footballs and helmet away. Tucker called it "some gamesmanship" and said he was preparing for the game.

The earlier exchange ended without a lasting dispute, but it established a pattern: Kelce reacted strongly when kicking work crosses into the Chiefs' warmup area. The Broncos incident adds another example without confirming formal fallout.

title: Will NASCAR Cup return to Mexico? Daniel Suárez explains the logistics and obstacles
description: After the 2025 Cup Series visit to Mexico City, Daniel Suárez assesses the operational challenges of staging the round again.
fullText:
The NASCAR Cup Series held its first official race in Latin America in 2025 when the top division of stock cars visited Mexico City at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, a competition that was not renewed for 2026 and is also not being considered for 2027.

However, Mexican driver Daniel Suárez does not rule out the possibility that the NASCAR Cup could visit Mexico again. Ahead of this Saturday's race on the Bristol oval, the Spire team member spoke with Motorsport.com about the logistical complications and commercial interests surrounding a race of this kind, which will be the first obstacles to resolve in order to repeat the experience.

Despite the enthusiasm of the fans and the series, Suárez explained that organising a Cup Series race outside the United States involves complex dynamics with local promoters, especially in Mexico, where the circuit in the capital operates as a venue for other types of events.

"It is very difficult to put on a NASCAR event or any kind of race at these venues because I learned a lot with NASCAR coming to Mexico. The way it works is that they have these places, they put on all these concerts and events, and they make a lot of money from that. But when it comes to racing, you need many weeks to prepare the race, and those are weeks when they can't have other kinds of events," Daniel Suárez told Motorsport.com.

The Monterrey native emphasised that, although there is willingness on both sides, the calendars have to align and lessons must be learned from the first experience:

"It takes a lot of planning to be able to put on an event like this and a lot of people involved. That's why I think there are different interest. NASCAR wants to come back and Mexico, as a country, they want NASCAR to return. They just have to connect the dots to make it possible and also learn from everything that happened last year, because there are many things that we as an industry could maybe have done a little better."

Asked whether venues closer to the border, such as his native Monterrey, could lessen the logistical burden given their proximity to the United States border, Suárez acknowledged and reiterated that the capital remains the ideal setting:

"It could be. Where I'm from in Monterrey, Mexico is only a couple of hours from Texas. Champ Car used to race there; in fact, that was the first race I attended. But that saves us, or saves the teams, maybe nine or ten hours of travel, so it's not much. I would say the main thing is the logistics, the promotion and everything we have to do around the event to make it a success. Personally, I think Mexico City is the heart of Mexico, that's where the great circuit like the Hermanos Rodríguez is, which has a strong name, and that's where it should be."

title: Iowa State football cruises against Bowling Green | Hines takeaways
description: Iowa State football had little trouble with Bowling Green. Columnist Travis Hines gives his initial thoughts on the victory.
fullText:
AMES – Iowa State football will head into Big 12 play riding high.

The Cyclones shrugged off their Cy-Hawk rivalry loss to Iowa last week with a dominating 55-7 effort to easily dispatch Bowling Green on Saturday, Sept. 19, at Jack Trice Stadium.

It was mostly a picturesque performance from Iowa State (2-1) against a hugely overmatched Bowling Green (0-3). The Cyclones completely controlled all three phases of the game and never gave the Falcons a moment of hope.

Aiden Flora rushed for nearly 200 yards despite watching from the sideline much of the second half, while the Cyclone defense continued its trend of high-level play, rarely surrendering much of anything to Bowling Green.

The win may not change the calculus of how Iowa State is perceived heading into its Big 12 slate (starting next weekend at home against No. 17 Utah), but it is further evidence that the Cyclones will be able to hold their own, despite the turnover from last year's roster.

It's difficult to imagine a better way to head into conference play than what the Cyclones showed against Bowling Green. Here are three takeaways from Saturday's big win.

We spent all week saying it would be nice for the Iowa State offense – particularly its rushing attack – to flex some muscle against an inferior opponent.

Well, consider the muscles flexed.

Flora had  194 yards and two touchdowns on 12 rushing attempts while the Cyclones ran for a total of 365 yards.

The grading curve coming into the game was relatively steep considering Nebraska put up over 500 yards of total offense (264 rushing) and 56 points on the Falcons last week, but Iowa State still earns an 'A' for complete domination on the ground.

Not only did Flora look great, but the offensive line clearly and consistently dominated the line of scrimmage to bust him into the second level, where Bowling Green repeatedly failed to bring him down.

Really encouraging showing from the ground game.

More: Iowa State football's Aiden Flora has huge first half vs Bowling Green

Now, we're going to pick some nits

Iowa State quarterback Jaylen Raynor and the Cyclone passing game looked a little more rickety.

Raynor was 11 of 17 for 133 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He struggled with his accuracy and ball placement at times. The Cyclones' preference is going to be to lean on their running game this year, but it's undoubtedly going to need the passing game to deliver more than it currently is against the Big 12.

On a day when the running game goes wild? Hardly a footnote.

We'll start with special teams because they put points on the board, but Iowa State's defense was dominant on the day as well.

Cam Pettaway tallied a 100-yard kick return touchdown while Flora put a 66-yard punt return touchdown on the board as well.

Both players have track records as elite return men, so it's unsurprising to see them stand out, but it's hard to imagine a better day than a pair of return scores. In fact, Iowa State has never before had a kick and punt return TD in the same game.

Now, clearly, Bowling Green was overmatched, but Iowa State's ability to get the 'hidden yardage' of positive punt and kick returns is going to be a story to watch all season, especially if the offense is going to need some help.

And for the third-straight week, Iowa State's defense showed itself to be formidable.

Bowling Green managed just 186 yards while turning it over twice. The Falcons' only touchdown came on a play in which two Cyclones inadvertently collided in coverage (more on that in a moment).

It was not even a year ago when Jack Trice Stadium was left silent when tight end Ben Brahmer collapsed on the field, leaving everyone witnessing it hoping they'd never see such a sight again.

But the violence and danger of this game are never far away.

Jaheim Singletary, a senior defensive back transfer from Arkansas, was carted off the field in the first half on a stretcher with his head and neck immobilized.

The injury occurred when he blindly collided with a teammate in the defensive backfield.

Singletary was transported to a local hospital for observation and had movement in his extremities, according to an Iowa State spokesperson.

Here's hoping (praying, pulling and wishing, too) that Singletary will be just fine. The incident was a sobering reminder of what these players are risking every time they take the field.

Iowa State columnist Travis Hines has covered the Cyclones for the Des Moines Register and Ames Tribune since 2012. Contact him at thines@amestrib.com or (515) 284-8000. Follow him on X at @TravisHines21.

title: Ben Johnson believes Drew Brees' advice stuck with Caleb Williams
description: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson believes his quarterback Caleb Williams will benefit from the advice given to him by Drew Brees.
fullText:
Before last week's game against the Carolina Panthers, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams met with NFL Hall of Fame quarterback Drew Brees, who gave the former No. 1 pick strategic advice to improve his completion percentage.

That advice from Brees, which came in their production meeting during game week, was Brees telling Williams that, if he increases his completions by three each week in every game, he will see the rise in completion percentage that many critics are looking for.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson heard that advice that his young quarterback received and believed it helped lead the franchise star to have a standout performance in Week 1, where he finished with a 72% completion percentage. Johnson said he believes that advice will stick with Williams moving forward.

"You turn on our tape and that (Brees' advice), might've stuck with our guy a little bit, which was cool to see," Johnson said. "A couple checkdowns to the backs, a couple times were the primary wasn't there and you can see him reset to the middle of the field. I thought he had some really nice throwing lanes, smart with the football, and I think what showed up was on the scramble, we had a lot more production than what we may have had in the past."

Coming into his third season in the NFL, the biggest criticism of Williams has been his low completion percentage despite the fact he's able to come up clutch in close games, where he led an NFL record seven fourth-quarter comebacks last season. The advice from Brees is simple but could end up being some of the biggest advice for Williams in his entire career.
