title: Samuel 'caught off guard' on winning Davis Cup debut
description: Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery get Britain off to a winning start in their Davis Cup qualifying tie against Ecuador.
fullText:
Toby Samuel says he was "caught off guard" about how much his Davis Cup debut meant to him as he got Great Britain off to a winning start in their qualifying tie against Ecuador.

The 24-year-old overcame nerves to fight back from a set down against Andres Andrade and put the hosts in front at London's sold-out Copper Box Arena.

Team-mate Arthur Fery, playing on home soil for the first time since his astonishing run to the Wimbledon semi-finals, then gave Britain a 2-0 lead with a commanding 7-5 6-0 win over Alvaro Guillen Meza.

"It's a completely new experience for me playing Davis Cup and it definitely caught me off guard how much it meant to me going out there for my first time," Samuel, who has enjoyed a breakthrough 2026 season, told BBC Sport.

"It almost felt like a bigger deal than playing any Slam for me."

Samuel has made his debut at three Grand Slams and climbed from outside of the world's top 250 to 95th in the men's singles rankings in the past nine months.

He was only handed his chance to play in the opening Davis Cup singles on Friday after British number two Cameron Norrie pulled out of the tie with an arm injury.

His debut got off to a tricky start as Andrade, ranked 203rd in the world, won the opening four games without reply en route to taking the first set 6-4.

But Samuel recovered to successfully navigate a tight second set before storming through the decider in 28 minutes, dropping just one game to wrap up a 4-6 6-4 6-1 win.

"This was a big dream of mine and you could sort of tell because I got a bit nervous at the start, but I got myself going and I am so happy I got the job done for Great Britain," he said in his on-court interview.

Great Britain captain Leon Smith said he was impressed by Samuel's coolness under pressure during his Davis Cup debut.

"He was absolutely pumped to be selected, when I called him when I was in New York - you could tell the excitement down the phone," Smith told BBC Sport.

"Sometimes it's actually easier, in inverted commas, maybe playing away from home in that debut where there are less eyes on you, less expectations.

"When he went 4-0 down, what impressed me was he stayed calm and he was very good to talk to in the chair."

As Samuel made his way courtside to watch along with the raucous crowd, Fery made his first appearance for his country as the British number one.

Fery, who has risen to 36th in the world following his run to the last four at Wimbledon and the final at Winston-Salem, was forced to work hard in an enthralling hour-long opening set.

However, his quality soon shone through and he won eight games in a row to sweep aside world number 293 Guillen Meza.

"We're used to travelling alone the whole year and coming out as a team in front of all you of you guys today in London is unbelievable," Fery said to the crowd.

"The tennis schedule is pretty relentless and we are playing week after week so you have to keep that motivation high, but it's easy to keep that motivation when you are playing for your country and representing the GB colours in front of everyone here with a team like this."

Henry Patten and Neal Skupski can wrap up the best-of-five tie at the earliest opportunity if they triumph in Sunday's doubles from 12:00 BST.

If not, Fery and Samuel will have to return to the court for the reverse singles to try and secure Britain's place in the knockout stage for the first time since 2023.

The seven winners of this weekend's qualifying ties will join three-time defending champions Italy in the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna from 24 to 29 November.

Austria and South Korea booked their tickets to the quarter-finals on Saturday with victories over Belgium and India respectively.

title: Castellanos spitting claim overshadows West Ham's show of character
description: Millwall keeper Filip Marshcall alleges he was spat at by West Ham forward Taty Castellanos during their 2-2 draw.
fullText:
On a day when eyes were focused on The Den with a fear that a fierce football rivalry could see the supporters of Millwall and West Ham make the headlines, it was one of the players that sparked the controversy.

Taty Castellanos is at the centre of the storm, after it was alleged the 27-year-old West Ham forward spat at Millwall keeper Filip Marschall during a pulsating game which ended in a 2-2 draw and with the Hammers down to 10 men.

The controversy, which unfortunately took some of the shine off an incredible contest, occurred in the 65th minute with the Lions leading 2-0.

Marschall was waiting with the ball at his feet until he was closed down, only picking it up to launch a clearance as Castellanos raced forward to apply pressure.

TV cameras caught Marschall, 23, appearing to show Premier League referee Paul Tierney a spot on his shirt he claimed was spit.

After the game, broadcasters were told Millwall had lodged a complaint to the match officials.

Millwall boss Alex Neil and Hammers counterpart Nuno Espirito Santo both told reporters they had not seen the incident, which was on the far side of the pitch from the dugouts.

Neil said: "I haven't asked [Filip] about it, but it's like anything else. I'm sure there'll be footage of it - or not if it didn't happen.

"I'd be extremely surprised if Filip's made an accusation and nothing's happened. I'm sure the authorities will deal with it.

"I didn't know what had happened, I'd just seen Filip walking out with the ball and thinking 'Where's he going?'.

"And then the fourth official basically said that there was an accusation of spitting."

Nuno added: "I'm aware of the allegation. I didn't see the images, I didn't speak with Taty [Castellanos].

"I cannot go much further on that, I'm sorry. For me to answer that, I have to see it. I'm going to look at the images. I cannot answer."

Spitting offences typically come with a six-match ban, if proven.

West Ham come from two goals down to secure derby draw at Millwall

Neil: 'Best atmosphere I've seen at the Den!'

The incident was a blot on a positive second half from the Hammers, who changed shape and intensity to wipe out a two-goal deficit.

Nuno told BBC Radio London: "It was a tough, tough game. We didn't start very well, it was a very intense atmosphere and we didn't deal with the physicality.

"The second half we improved in our game. Our passing was better. The players showed up - I'm happy for that but I'm disappointed we didn't stick to the plan.

"In the end our fans were happy, not in the way they wanted. But the way the game went I think it's a positive result."

The Portuguese said the three-week international break comes at a good time for the Hammers, who can work on the defensive fragility which led to both Millwall goals.

"We are learning [about this division] but we can't waste much time," he added. "We are being punished with the physicality.

"Just look at the goals we are conceding from throw-ins, it's worrying. This international break will be very useful for us."

title: Britain beat Germany to win World Championship bronze
description: Great Britain men's team win bronze at the Wheelchair Basketball World Championships by defeating Germany, but GB women lose out in third-place play-off.
fullText:
Great Britain men's team won bronze at the Wheelchair Basketball World Championships by defeating Germany 67-56 in the third-place play-off.

After conceding an early lead in Ottawa, GB scored twice in less than a minute and stayed in front from then on, with Gregg Warburton leading his side's scoring with 20 points.

The outcome means Britain's men have won a medal at three consecutive World Championships after taking gold and silver at the 2018 and 2022 editions.

GB women missed out on a medal as they lost 63-50 to the Netherlands in their third-place match.

Britain, captained by Sophie Carrigill, trailed after two periods but levelled the scoring at 44-44 heading into the final quarter of the match.

The Netherlands, champions in 2018 and 2022, then stepped it up and dominated the closing quarter 19-6 to secure another medal.

Fourth place is still a big improvement for GB women, who finished ninth at the 2022 edition of the tournament.

title: FAA clears proposed Trump arch, requires 'eternal flame' to alert pilots
description:
The Federal Aviation Administration said on Friday a proposed triumphal arch President Donald Trump wants to build near Arlington National Cemetery ‌in Washington would not pose a hazard to aircraft but would be required to ‌have an "eternal flame" on top. 
   The FAA determination requires it to be marked with a light on top of the structure and ​floodlight projectors pointed at the arch to make it noticeable for pilots. Some aviation experts have raised safety concerns given its proximity to Reagan Washington National Airport. 
   The determination clears an aviation hurdle for the arch, which Trump proposed to mark the nation's 250th anniversary. The project is part of the ‌president's broader drive to reshape ⁠Washington's monumental landscape, including a new White House ballroom, renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and redevelopment of a golf course in East Potomac ⁠Park.
fullText:
WASHINGTON, Sept 18 (Reuters) - The Federal Aviation Administration said on Friday a proposed triumphal arch President Donald Trump wants to build near Arlington National Cemetery ‌in Washington would not pose a hazard to aircraft but would be required to ‌have an "eternal flame" on top.

The FAA determination requires it to be marked with a light on top of the structure and ​floodlight projectors pointed at the arch to make it noticeable for pilots. Some aviation experts have raised safety concerns given its proximity to Reagan Washington National Airport.

The determination clears an aviation hurdle for the arch, which Trump proposed to mark the nation's 250th anniversary. The project is part of the ‌president's broader drive to reshape ⁠Washington's monumental landscape, including a new White House ballroom, renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and redevelopment of a golf course in East Potomac ⁠Park.

Veterans have sued to block the arch, arguing it would destroy the historic sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

The FAA previously said the arch would need red obstruction lights but said on Friday ​the ​structure no longer is required to have them.

The FAA ​determination is subject to review if ‌anyone petitions by October 18.

In June, US Senator Tammy Duckworth, the top Democrat on the Senate aviation subcommittee, urged the FAA to reject White House pressure to approve the proposed 250-foot (76-meter) arch, saying it could pose risks to commercial flights.

The proposed arch would be 3,000 feet from Washington National Airport and within the airport's main approach and departure corridor.

The FAA generally requires blinking red warning ‌lights on buildings above 200 feet near airports to ​warn pilots at night, like on the nearby 555-foot-tall Washington ​Monument.

Duckworth cited the National Park Service ​as saying construction of Trump's arch would require cranes reaching 300 to 320 ‌feet in height and could last 20 hours ​per day for two ​to three years.

The FAA said pilots must fly at least 780 feet above the area around the arch, at least 488 feet above the top of the proposed structure.

On ​September 4, a federal judge ordered ‌the Trump administration to give 48 hours' notice before engaging in any activity on ​the arch site, except for work to identify underground cultural artifacts.

title: A rare, high-elevation tornado hits Utah mountainside at nearly 7,500 feet
description:
When you're living near a mountainside, one of the last things you would expect to see moving fast at higher elevations would be a tornado, but that's what happened in Utah on Friday.
According to the Salt Lake City, Utah, branch of the U.S. National Weather Service (NWS), a rare, strong twister occurred near Fruit Heights, Utah. The funnel first made contact
with the ground near a summit along the ridgeline extending west from Francis Peak, at an elevation of about 7,500 feet (almost 2,300 metres).
fullText:
When you're living near a mountainside, one of the last things you would expect to see moving fast at higher elevations would be a tornado, but that's what happened in Utah on Friday.

According to the Salt Lake City, Utah, branch of the U.S. National Weather Service (NWS), a rare, strong twister occurred near Fruit Heights, Utah. The funnel first made contact
with the ground near a summit along the ridgeline extending west from Francis Peak, at an elevation of about 7,500 feet (almost 2,300 metres).

Tornadoes are uncommon at very high elevation due to drier air and less favourable thunderstorm dynamics.

Brittany Whitlam, a NWS meteorologist who works at the Salt Lake City office, told Newsweek that radar signatures showed the twister lofted debris 4,000 feet into the air.

She also noted that, based on the radar and videos sent in from residents in the area, NWS can confirm it was a "strong" tornado, but there won't be an official rating designated until a survey team is deployed to the scene to review any damage incurred.

As well, a second tornado struck south of Vernal, Utah.

title: New Zealand cruise to victory over Scotland in WXV
description: Scotland suffer a second successive defeat in the WXV Global Series as New Zealand run out comfortable winners at Hive Stadium.
fullText:
Tries: Gallagher 2 Cons: Nelson 2

Tries: Palu, Vaipulu, McGregor, King, Sae 2, Du Plessis, Sititi, Turner, Saili Cons: Sorensen-McGree 7, King

Scotland suffered a second successive defeat in the WXV Global Series as New Zealand ran out comfortable winners at Hive Stadium.

The Black Ferns ran in 10 tries while the Scots struggled to contain the number two ranked team in the world.

New Zealand took no time at all to exert their dominance, punching holes in the Scottish defence before powerful prop Mo'omo'oga Palu blasted through to score.

The Black Ferns set a tempo the Scots could just not live with, and another foray into the Scottish 22 resulted in a neat finish from lock Maama Mo'onia Vaipulu for the second try.

Chloe Rollie picked off an intercept to get Scotland down the pitch and force a penalty, and from the resulting line-out the ball was shipped to Evie Gallagher to crash over.

The visitors reasserted their authority with tries from Justine McGregor and Elinor-Plum King, but the Scots showed some guts to fashion another close-range try for Gallagher to keep them in the game at 24-14.

However, their defensive frailties were exposed as Layla Sae and Amy Du Plessis struck with superb tries to effectively end the game as a contest before half-time.

It bore many of the hallmarks of last weekend's defeat by Canada, with the Scots conceding immediately any time they looked to have found a way back into the match.

The visitors put their foot on the gas after the break with substitute Amarante Sititi and Tara Turner going over before Sae added her second try, New Zealand's ninth.

To their credit, the Scots kept the Black Ferns scoreless from the 47th minute until the final play when Alena Saili crossed for New Zealand's 10th try to round off a dominant display.

Next up for Scotland is Australia back at Hive Stadium next Saturday (16:10), while New Zealand will head south to face England on the same day (15:00).

fullText:
WASHINGTON, Sept 19 (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump said in a social media post on Saturday that he plans to appoint a new artificial intelligence adviser, known as ‌an "AI czar," and create an "AI force," though he did not provide details about either ‌initiative or how they would be implemented.

Fears are growing in Washington among lawmakers about the risks posed by AI technology on ​humans and property. Earlier this month, former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon said that "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade." Trump has repeatedly downplayed concerns about AI and argued that additional regulation is unnecessary.

"We will not in any way hinder or stifle ‌the Growth of this incredible Industry," ⁠Trump wrote on Truth Social, his social media platform. "Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows! However, we will also ⁠be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System."

If Trump follows through on the pledge, it would be his second AI czar. Venture ​capitalist David ​Sacks previously served in the role before stepping down ​in the spring and moving into ‌an external advisory position.

Sacks has echoed Trump's skepticism of new AI regulation. Speaking at a Politico event on Wednesday, he said AI developers should be responsible for ensuring the safety of their products and could be held liable if problems arise, adding that new federal rules are unnecessary.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Trump's post.

Trump's post comes ahead ‌of his scheduled meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on ​Thursday. Washington and Beijing are competing for leadership in ​artificial intelligence, which both governments view as ​vital to their economic and military strength. Trump and technology executives have argued ‌that excessive regulation would slow US AI development and ​undermine American companies' ability ​to compete with Chinese rivals, a claim that safety advocates often refute.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will meet with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng on Sunday at JPMorgan Chase headquarters in ​New York to discuss AI ‌security, trade and other economic issues, a person familiar with the planning said on ​Saturday.

fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Several of the nation's largest left-leaning voter engagement and racial justice organizations are facing steep funding shortfalls and staffing cutbacks just as voting is getting underway in an election that will determine control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump's term.

The shortfalls are setting off alarms among Democratic strategists, who are betting on high turnout and robust voter protection efforts to boost the party's chances this fall. They are worried that many grassroots groups will not be able to mount effective registration and get-out-the-vote efforts, much less protect against the possibility of election interference from the Republican administration.

America Votes, a coordinating hub for more than 400 progressive groups, has fallen "well below" the level of funding it had during the 2022 midterms, Daria Dawson, America Votes' executive director, said in a statement to The Associated Press. America Votes has acted as a nerve center for the voter mobilization efforts of groups such as the NAACP, Planned Parenthood, the League of Conservation Voters, the AFL-CIO and SEIU labor unions, as well as local groups focused on racial justice, climate and civil liberties.

"There is still time to reach voters and bring them into this election, but we are no longer talking about a future opportunity," Dawson said. "The window to engage them is open now, and it is narrowing every day."

Wealthy donors and philanthropic groups have reduced their support of many liberal causes since the 2024 presidential election. That pullback has been especially stark for voting groups geared toward engaging communities of color.

While multiple organizers said some funders had expressed an interest in adopting different strategies, racial justice organizers have felt that as a betrayal.

A retreat in donor support is "handcuffing our ability to persuade our communities to vote in a year where there is no Voting Rights Act," said Esosa Osa, a veteran Democratic strategist and founder of Onyx Impact, a research group focused on combating misinformation in Black communities.

The Supreme Court this year knocked out one of the last remaining pillars of that landmark 1965 law, essentially gutting it.

"We are watching surrender, not strategy," Osa said.

A July memo circulated among major Democratic fundraisers warned that "the organizations that registered and persuaded millions of voters to participate in the 2018 and 2022 midterms are drastically underfunded. They have raised nearly 40% less than they had at this point in those cycles."

It further warned that funding voter mobilization groups was especially critical "given that the Democratic brand is underperforming on generic ballot tests relative to historical comparisons and the president's approval ratings."

The shortfalls have led organizations focused on engaging and mobilizing key voting groups to scale back operations and staffing over the last year. That has included programs aimed at registering and mobilizing lower-propensity voters, voters of color, and rural and younger voters.

The Democratic National Committee, which has faced its own funding challenges, has consolidated voter engagement efforts this year partly in response to the ecosystem's past shortcomings. The DNC in a statement said it was making "historic investments" in its organizing but did not address the weaknesses among allied groups.

"We are expanding our voter protection infrastructure to defend Americans' sacred right to vote, hold Trump and Republicans accountable in court, and register and mobilize voters across the country," said Angelo Fernández Hernández, a DNC spokesperson.

The reasons for the troubled funding landscape are varied and at times unclear, according to nearly two dozen fundraisers and organizers who spoke with the AP. Some donors, still disappointed with the Democratic Party and some of its allies following the 2024 presidential election, have closed their pocketbooks to liberal causes entirely.

While a small group of liberal megadonors has continued to bankroll progressive causes, most focus their support on liberal legal organizations that have taken the Trump administration to court, rather than political or voter engagement groups.

Others, including major philanthropic institutions, have pulled back out of fear of retribution that giving to political or racial justice causes could draw the administration's ire. Organizers who have engaged with potential donors said the administration's targeting of political opponents and diversity initiatives seems to have put a chill on fundraising for their causes.

Tameka Ramsey-Brown, founding director of the Michigan Coalition on Black Civic Participation, said multiple donors since the 2024 election had asked whether her group could remove the word "Black" from its name or find financial conduits to mask the source of donations for fear of retribution from the administration.

"Just being Black in this country again has become a bad word, and it has made it that much more difficult just to raise money because funders don't want the added pressure and stress or attacks on them by funding us," she said.

Many of the nonprofit groups that traditionally have conducted the registration, voter education and organizing say they are trying to adapt to their new, leaner reality.

Vamos a Votar, an initiative of the largest civil rights and advocacy groups focused on Latino communities, has had to readjust its ambitions this year due to a lack of investment from funders.

"This is shaping up to be a cycle where investments haven't gone to the Black and brown communities that will ultimately decide this election," said Juan Proaño, CEO of the League of United Latin American Citizens, a member of the initiative.

In a September pitch circulated among donors, the coalition said it aimed to invest $27.5 million in voter engagement and persuasion efforts this year, but still required $5.4 million from donors to fund voter turnout efforts across 10 states and 17 House districts. Even that investment reflected reduced ambitions from previous pitches to donors early this year.

"It has been extremely disappointing to see that progressive donors are not meeting the moment," said Héctor Sánchez Barba, the CEO of Mi Familia Vota, one of the affiliated organizations. "We are not waiting. We are always on the front lines for our democracy and our communities."

To counter the funding cutbacks, some groups have begun relying more heavily on artificial intelligence to provide voter registration guides, share information in multiple languages and track potential election issues. Some groups have increased their partnerships with ride-sharing companies to provide free rides to polling places instead of bus shuttles.

With fewer in-person organizers, some groups are also focusing on social media and partnering with liberal content creators to boost their messages.

"In my more than 30 years of organizing, it has never been this bad to raise money to support Black causes of any kind," said Melanie Campbell, president and CEO of the National Coalition on Black Civic Participation, a nonpartisan civil rights group. "We're going to do the work, our state affiliates are doing all that is possible. ... But the bottom line is that those who believe that democracy matters should make sure they fund the work."

title: Ashton hat-trick helps Warrington end Hull KR reign
description: Matty Ashton scores a hat-trick as Warrington Wolves beat Hull Kingston Rovers in the Super League play-off eliminators.
fullText:
Betfred Super League play-off eliminator

Tries: Currie, Ashton 3, Hopoate, King Goals: Irwin 5 Drop-goal: Williams

Tries: Burgess, Hadley Goals: Mourgue 2

Matty Ashton scored a hat-trick as Warrington Wolves ended Hull Kingston Rovers' reign as Super League champions with victory in the play-off eliminator.

Wire will now travel to play Leeds Rhinos at AMT Headingley on Friday, 25 September for a place in the Grand Final, with Wakefield Trinity taking on Wigan Warriors in the other semi-final the following evening.

Warrington were the better side throughout but only held a 12-6 lead at half-time as a superb Joe Burgess try for the Robins answered scores from Ben Currie and Ashton.

The task became much tougher for Willie Peters' side, who managed a clean sweep of domestic honours last season, when Peta Hiku was sent off after his fist to the face of George Williams was deemed to be a punch.

Ashton's second try brought a response from Dean Hadley but the Wolves ran away with it as Ashton grabbed his third, Albert Hopoate and Toby King also crossed, and Williams capped a fine display with a late drop-goal.

Warrington beat Hull KR in eliminator - as it happened

Defeat brought Peters' successful reign as Rovers coach to an end, as he leaves to join new NRL franchise PNG Chiefs next season, and his team produced an underwhelming display which reflected their inconsistent season.

They finished eight points behind the Wolves in the Super League table and that gap was evident as Burgess's early fumble gifted Currie a try under the posts, with Ewan Irwin converting and then adding a penalty as Sam Burgess's side dominated.

The Robins briefly showed the style which brought them last season's Super League title, the League Leaders' Shield and Challenge Cup as Arthur Mourgue broke from close to his own line and Joe Burgess was in support to score a try that took them within two points.

Wire's response was instant as they carved open the Robins' right flank and Ashton finished for his 100th Super League try, although Rovers fans still had belief that their side could turn it around in the second half.

Those hopes evaporated as Hiku stupidly thrust his closed fist in the face of a startled Williams, and a video review deemed it to be a red card offence.

Rovers continued to battle as Karl Lawton thrust his foot under the ball to prevent a Josh Thewlis try and Hadley went up the other end to take the 12 men to within four points.

Hadley seemed set to level the scores as he strode for the posts but James Bentley stole the ball and broke, and when the pacy Ashton got up in support, there was only going to be one outcome as he claimed his third of the night.

That deflated a resurgent Robins side and Hopoate produced a spectacular acrobatic finish, Williams added a one-pointer and King said farewell to the Halliwell Jones Stadium on his final home appearance before joining London Broncos with a late try to round off a comprehensive win.

title: Brighton humbling 'a big lesson' for Arsenal - Arteta
description: An uncharacteristic performance from Arsenal saw the Gunners ship three goals in the defeat to Brighton - but could the loss be the "big lesson" they needed?
fullText:
An uncharacteristic performance from Arsenal saw them ship three goals at Brighton - but boss Mikel Arteta believes their first Premier League defeat this season could prove a "big lesson".

The defending champions have been tipped by many to retain the title they won last season for the first time in 22 years.

An impressive seven-match winning start to this campaign in all competitions - nine in successive league games dating back to April - backed up that belief.

But Arsenal were humbled on the south coast as a well-drilled and clinical Brighton outfit beat them comfortably 3-0 to go third in the table.

Arteta, whose side did not lose by more than a single goal in the top flight last term, acknowledged the Seagulls "deserved" the success and there were lessons the Gunners needed to take heading into the international break.

The manner of the defeat - Arsenal's heaviest in a season where they were the reigning top-flight champions since 1989 - will also offer hope to their title rivals that they are not invincible.

Arsenal handed first loss by brilliant Brighton

Since taking charge in 2019, Arteta has made a point of reiterating how much he values physicality and the demands he puts on his side to win duels.

But against Brighton, Arsenal were dominated all over the pitch and lost challenges which they would usually be expected to win.

Arteta said he was "extremely disappointed" as his side were "very far" from doing the basics he expected, with uncertainty in defence, a loss of midfield control and lack of attacking creativity.

Asked why they were below par, the Spaniard added: "Well, the first one because Brighton they were really good, and they had another bite, and at the times it was better.

"There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50-50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.

"Sometimes there were some technical errors very much involved that opened us up in a really difficult way, but that's something to learn."

He was quick to remind the media in his news conference after the game that it was still a good start to the season.

The Gunners had 15 players at the World Cup which meant that a large part of the squad joined up for pre-season later than the rest of their team-mates.

"That's not going to take away what the team has done and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup," added Arteta.

"What we've done and the way we've competed and the amount of games we've won has been remarkable, but this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level."

Brighton are currently the Premier League's top scorers with 16 goals - hitting eight of them in the past week - and could have had more against an Arsenal side who pride themselves on keeping clean sheets.

The Gunners conceded the fewest goals of any side last season and just one got past David Raya in their first four league games before Saturday's defeat.

"It should have been more, the chances Brighton created, they were that good," said former Newcastle striker Alan Shearer on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"They absolutely battered Arsenal. How many times have we said that recently? From start to finish today Brighton were magnificent, every single one of them played their part.

"They were strong, they were fit, they went after Arsenal. They had no fear and it worked brilliantly for them, it should have been six or seven goals."

The Gunners were 2-0 down at the break and have not recovered to win from such a position in a league game since March 2008 at Bolton.

"Every time Brighton chased down the ball, they got it absolutely spot on. They did it as a team, they didn't do it individually," added Shearer.

"They thought, 'we respect Arsenal but we're not going to give them any space to play'.

"The organisation was great and that just doesn't happen on it's own and you've got to give [manager] Fabian Hurzeler credit for that."

Arsenal spent around £200m in the summer transfer window in a bid to strengthen the squad to challenge for more honours, and Arteta was asked if they needed reminding how tough the Premier League can be.

He said: "I think they knew, I think we knew how tough it was going to be today, and the first thing that we had discussed was about the first part.

"If you don't get out of that first part as winners, it will be extremely difficult to dominate the game and to have any probability of winning the game.

"We knew that, but that's again credit to them for what they've done because they've overcome us and they had another edge than we did.

"And that's something that at this level it's extremely important to respect and to understand before anything else."

Former Premier League defender Curtis Davies believed the Gunners could put the result and display down to a "blip".

"Their form this season has so far been good, this has been a really shocking performance," he said on 5 Live.

"That defence today was nowhere near what it's used to being. The disappointment will be a set-piece goal conceded, Arsenal will have a real long look at themselves.

"They didn't lay a glove on Brighton, and didn't make anything of their attacking situations."

title: England crush Sri Lanka to top T20 world rankings
description: England steamroller Sri Lanka in the third T20 to complete a 3-0 series clean sweep and return to number one in the world rankings.
fullText:
Third T20 international, Old Trafford

Sri Lanka 124 all out (18.5 overs): Nissanka 36 (24), K Mendis 35 (28); Baker 2-17, Archer 2-23, Jacks 2-31

England 126-2 (9.4 overs): Buttler 62* (32), Brook 33 (21)

England won by eight wickets, won series 3-0

England steamrollered Sri Lanka in the third T20 to complete a 3-0 series clean sweep and return to number one in the world rankings.

Watched by new Test coach Stephen Fleming, England once again outclassed the tourists to conclude a one-sided series played on the fringe of autumn.

England's pace bowlers were outstanding in dismissing Sri Lanka for a paltry 124, then the home side chased the target in 9.4 overs.

Jamie Overton conceded only 15 runs in his four overs, including taking a wicket. Sonny Baker's improvement continued with 2-17 and Jofra Archer recovered from an expensive start to return 2-23.

England's fielding was sharp, best demonstrated by Liam Dawson's direct hit to run out Eshan Malinga.

The target was never likely to pose a challenge to an England batting line-up that remains powerful despite Phil Salt and Jacob Bethell being absent injured.

Though opener Aneurin Donald was out for 13, Jos Buttler and Harry Brook strolled the pursuit with a second-wicket stand of 85.

Brook was run out for 33, leaving Buttler to wrap it up with a six that left him unbeaten on 61.

The victory by eight wickets was concluded with 62 balls to spare - the most for England in a home T20 international.

The success was England's 23rd win in 26 completed T20s since Brook took charge in the summer of 2024. They have reclaimed their number one ranking from India.

The pity for this group is a rare lengthy wait until the next global T20 tournament. The next men's T20 World Cup is not until 2028, the same year T20 cricket makes its debut in the Olympics.

England are instead building towards a 50-over World Cup in southern Africa in the autumn of 2027. Three one-day internationals against the Sri Lankans begin in Durham on Tuesday.

Buttler crunches 62 not out as England seal 3-0 series win - as it happened

A feature of England's success in this format has been captain Brook's heavy use of spin bowling. On this occasion the spinners took a backseat – Adil Rashid and Dawson sent down only four overs between them.

Instead, it was the seamers to the fore, even without the variations of Sam Curran, another England player absent injured.

Baker endured difficult debuts in all three international formats, yet in this series has started to show his potential.

After Archer's first over went for 15, Baker had Lahiru Udara sky to wicketkeeper Buttler. He later returned to wrap up the innings, taking the final wicket when Dilshan Madushanka skied to Brook.

Archer was a spectator for some time after his initial struggle. When he returned, he got the dangerous Kamindu Mendis to pull to deep mid-wicket for 35.

Archer's second wicket was curious – Wanindu Hasaranga out hit-wicket attempting a slog, his bat almost placed on top of the bails.

Overton was the pick, returning his most economical figures when bowling his full allocation of four in a T20 international.

Though Tom Banton dropped a catch slipping on the greasy outfield, England's fielding was otherwise exceptional.

Brook took a sharp catch at mid-wicket to remove Pathum Nissanka for 36, Rashid was alert enough to run out Charith Asalanka and Dawson's direct hit was the coup de grace.

At the age of 29, Donald has been given an international opportunity in this series as a replacement for Salt.

He has shown only glimpses of his excellent domestic form, returning a high score of 21. On this occasion, he tried to wallop the spin of Tharindu Rathnayake over long-on and was stumped by a distance.

In Buttler and Brook, the captains past and present, England have two men in supreme form. Buttler is England's best white-ball batter of all-time, while Brook is on the way to being one of their greats.

Such is their quality, the second-wicket pair turned the remainder of the chase into little more than a glorified net.

Sri Lanka were scruffy – they conceded 17 runs in wides. The hapless nature of the visitors' display was epitomised when Brook should have been caught off Madushanka, only for keeper Kamil Mishara and point fielder Nissanka to look at each other as the ball dropped to the ground.

There was no need for Brook to attempt a single that Hasaranga fielded in his follow-through, the bowler hitting direct with a throw at the non-striker's end.

Buttler won it in the following over, clubbing 18 from four Malinga deliveries, with two maximums hammered over the leg side.

title: 'Greater things to come' says Mitchell after England winning run ends
description: Head coach John Mitchell says England's thrilling draw with Canada will inspire "greater things to come" from the world champions despite the result ending their record-breaking winning streak.
fullText:
Head coach John Mitchell believes England's thrilling draw with Canada will inspire "greater things to come" from the world champions despite the result ending their record-breaking winning streak.

England had won their past 39 Tests before Saturday's fixture.

Canada, who had lost their 13 previous meetings with the Red Roses on English soil, held England to a 26-26 draw in a nail-biting, physical battle at Exeter's Sandy Park.

It was only the second game domestically or internationally for England's players this season and, for Mitchell, one result is not justification to tear up the playbook.

Instead, he views it as a building block towards future success.

"It was just a matter of scoring across the white line," Mitchell said. "We were applying huge pressure. We just didn't convert."

Avoiding defeat means the Red Roses have extended their unbeaten run to 40 matches, a record they will hope to extend with WXV Global Series games against New Zealand, two more fixtures against Canada and another against the United States still to come.

Mitchell said: "There was such good stuff in there. I'm very patient because we're just starting and we're still alive in this Test series.

"I'm a realist. There will be greater things come as a result of this. There's a greater purpose and one Test match is not going to take us away from our purpose."

For the opening 10 minutes, the match followed the script of last year's World Cup final between the two sides, with Canada breaking the deadlock and England immediately hitting back.

But unlike last September, when they roared on to win 33-13, the Red Roses could not maintain control, with the two teams never separated by more than one try and England unable to convert 20 minutes of sustained pressure into the crucial score.

While acknowledging England would have to review their "game management", captain Meg Jones hailed the spectacle the two sides delivered.

"It was definitely tit for tat and definitely a game of momentum swinging," said centre Jones. "It was two good teams going at each other.

"It was an amazing contest and competitive as we imagined. This is the first Test. We get another two shots at it [against Canada]."

Echoing Jones' defiance before October trips to Toronto and Ottawa, Mitchell added: "We're in a Test series. It's 1-1. That's it."

England's 39-game winning run started under former head coach Simon Middleton, who, after the World Cup final defeat in 2022, led the Red Roses to a Women's Six Nations Grand Slam in 2023.

Mitchell then took charge midway through the 2023 WXV1 campaign and had won every game until this one.

England beat Scotland in the World Cup quarter-finals last September to claim their 31st straight Test win, surpassing their own record winning streak across both men's and women's international rugby union, which was set in 2022.

World Cup glory, another Women's Six Nations title and victory over Australia last weekend extended that record further.

"It's not necessarily something we speak about as a group; it's something that's just been there," Jones said of the winning run.

"We're very process-driven, so the outcome tends to look after itself."

Northern Ireland's world number two made a superb eagle three on the 18th to stay in contention with a three-under 69, leaving him on 11 under.

title: Map shows border wall progress as new work begins
description:
New panels for the border wall are being installed in West Texas, marking the start of visible construction on a 47.3-mile project in the Big Bend region as President Donald Trump’s administration expands its barrier network along the southern border.
U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) said the first panels for the Big Bend 1 project in Hudspeth County went up on September 15, the Associated Press first reported.
fullText:
New panels for the border wall are being installed in West Texas, marking the start of visible construction on a 47.3-mile project in the Big Bend region as President Donald Trump’s administration expands its barrier network along the southern border.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) said the first panels for the Big Bend 1 project in Hudspeth County went up on September 15, the Associated Press first reported.

Work is beginning amid legal challenges and resistance from landowners concerned about the federal government’s plans for the remote region.

The development gives new significance to CBP’s Smart Wall map, which records 232.4 miles of various border infrastructure completed since January 20, 2025, and shows hundreds more moving through design or construction.

Newsweek contacted CBP on Saturday morning via email for further comment.

Trump directed federal agencies in January 2025 to construct temporary and permanent physical barriers supported by personnel and technology.

CBP said it is using $46.5 billion from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act to develop what it calls the “Smart Wall.”

The latest work extends that program into a part of Texas where rugged terrain and private ownership have historically limited continuous fencing.

CBP’s plans can affect landowners, border communities and visitors to public spaces through new walls, roads, surveillance equipment and vehicle barriers.

Big Bend 1 is one component of CBP’s plan for approximately 175 miles of primary barrier across Hudspeth, Jeff Davis and Presidio counties.

Agency planning documents say the system may include surveillance cameras, lighting, fiber-optic and power cables, utility shelters, and access and patrol roads.

Work has moved forward first near Sierra Blanca, east of El Paso.

The other two primary wall projects shown on CBP’s map cover 62.2 miles and 56.3 miles respectively, but reporting published on September 18 said construction had not begun on those Presidio County sections.

Access to private land presents a significant complication.

Some property owners are challenging the administration’s use of eminent domain and environmental-law waivers, potentially leaving the government able to build on certain parcels but not others.

Clara Bensen of the No Big Bend Wall coalition told The Guardian that officials were moving forward even though “the plan is not fully baked,” while land disputes complicate efforts to construct a continuous barrier.

Newsweek reached out to the campaign group for further comment via email on Saturday morning.

Bob Krumenaker, a former Big Bend National Park superintendent who chairs Keep Big Bend Wild, said in The Guardian opposition had crossed party lines: “I’m very optimistic that there is a lot of support for Big Bend. This is a nonpartisan issue.”

A coalition of West Texas landowners has also filed a federal lawsuit shortly before the construction update, seeking to stop projects across the region.

CBP has published a live interactive Smart Wall map that allows people to explore individual projects and view their construction status. You can see the live map here.

CBP’s map depicts a collection of different enforcement structures, not one uninterrupted wall.

The map uses color-coded lines to distinguish bollard, vehicle and waterborne barriers from supporting infrastructure and technology-only sections without a wall.

Red marks bollard barriers, orange vehicle barriers, blue waterborne barriers, purple system attributes only; light green technology and patrol roads without a wall; and dark green technology-only coverage without a wall or road.

The categories reflect the wider mix of barriers, roads and detection technology included in CBP’s Smart Wall program.

For new primary Smart Wall, the agency lists 357.4 miles under construction, 193.1 miles awarded and 70 miles completed. Another 417.2 miles of secondary wall are being built, while 88.5 miles are awarded and 72.1 miles are finished.

Waterborne systems represent another major category, with 375.2 miles under construction, 115.4 miles awarded and 42.1 miles complete.

Replacement of existing primary barriers accounts for a smaller share.

Those figures cannot simply be combined and described as a single length of new wall.

Primary fencing, parallel secondary structures and river barriers may occupy the same general locations.

Terminology matters too. CBP uses “under construction” when wall panels or waterborne barriers are being built or deployed.

“Awarded” may mean a project remains in design, although it can also cover early construction activity.

CBP said it does not intend to install 30-foot steel bollard walls inside Big Bend National Park, Big Bend Ranch State Park or the Black Gap Wildlife Management Area.

Cameras, sensors and low-profile vehicle barriers are planned instead.

That distinction means construction in Hudspeth County should not be conflated with separate work proposed inside the national park.

CBP said it is coordinating with the National Park Service to maintain access to the Rio Grande and hiking trails while identifying cultural, historical and biological resources that could be affected.

The plans have drawn public protests in and around Big Bend National Park, including demonstrations at Santa Elena Canyon on August 12 and in Study Butte, Texas, on August 15, as residents and public lands advocates raised concerns about construction in the protected landscape.

Demonstrators gathered with signs opposing border infrastructure in one of West Texas’ best-known protected landscapes.

Physical barriers make up only part of the program. CBP plans approximately 538 miles of technology beside previously built barriers and about 205 miles of detection equipment near Big Bend vehicle barriers.

A further 167 miles of the border are expected to receive separately funded detection technology because terrain or remoteness makes wall construction unfavorable.

Combined with the Big Bend deployment, CBP says approximately 372 miles will be covered by technology alone.

The immediate questions are whether construction extends beyond the parcels now available to the government, how pending litigation affects the schedule and when the remaining Big Bend sections advance.

CBP cautions that mileage may change as designs and routes are finalized. Its map also does not provide project-level completion dates, final costs or independent measurements showing how each barrier type affects unlawful crossings, smuggling or migrant safety.

Newsweek’s reporters and editors used Martyn, our AI assistant, to produce this story. Learn more about Martyn here.

title: New poll puts James Talarico 6 points ahead of Ken Paxton in Texas Senate race
description:
A new Texas Pulse poll shows the Democrat widening his lead over the Republican in the Texas Senate race, with Election Day more than a month away.
Published Sept. 17, the ReconMR/Texas Pulse poll showed that Democrat James Talarico's lead has grown to 6 points — outside the poll's margin of error — over Republican Ken Paxton, 49%-43%.
“This movement can also be seen by looking at independent voters who now favor Talarico by 40 points, 64-24%, up from 23 points, 53-30% in July,” ReconMR Senior Research Analyst Lindsey Hendren said.
Here's a deeper look at the poll and how it compares to other September polls.
fullText:
A new Texas Pulse poll shows the Democrat widening his lead over the Republican in the Texas Senate race, with Election Day more than a month away.

Published Sept. 17, the ReconMR/Texas Pulse poll showed that Democrat James Talarico's lead has grown to 6 points — outside the poll's margin of error — over Republican Ken Paxton, 49%-43%.

“This movement can also be seen by looking at independent voters who now favor Talarico by 40 points, 64-24%, up from 23 points, 53-30% in July,” ReconMR Senior Research Analyst Lindsey Hendren said.

Here's a deeper look at the poll and how it compares to other September polls.

The latest Texas Pulse poll was conducted Sept. 8 to 11 among 614 likely Texas voters and has an overall margin of error of 4.3 percentage points.

The poll found that Paxton has a negative favorability rating — 38%-55% — down slightly from 40-52% in July. Talarico has a positive favorability rating of 50-39%, up from 46-39% in July.

When asked who they think will win the election, 48% of voters say Talarico while 45% say Paxton.

The poll also found another shift: a quarter of voters didn’t have an opinion about Talarico in June — now it’s just 10%.

“Paxton’s Senate bid is being undermined by defections from within his own party," Hendren said. "While nearly all Democrats say they are supporting Talarico, just under 9 in 10 Republicans say they are supporting Paxton."

This is the latest poll in September as the election cycle enters its final stretch to Election Day on Nov. 3.

Fever celebrate Kelsey Mitchell's record-breaking game with a postgame party
description: Following Kelsey Mitchell's achievement of the WNBA single-season scoring record, the Indiana Fever celebrated her with an locker-room party after the game.
fullText:
After setting the WNBA single-season scoring record, the Indiana Fever celebrated Kelsey Mitchell in a lively locker-room postgame party.

Mitchell's clutch three-pointer in the third quarter fueled her way to a 33-point performance, propelling the Fever to a 103-85 victory over the Toronto Tempo and securing the new WNBA season scoring record.

After the game, when Mitchell returned to the locker room, her teammates surprised her by popping confetti containers that showered her during the celebration as they chanted her name, 'Kelsey!'

After thanking her teammates, Mitchell jokingly asked, "What did I do?" Her teammates enthusiastically replied, "Single-season scoring record!" before breaking out in chants of 'MVP!'

With this performance, Mitchell's season total rose to 1,023 points, surpassing the previous record of 1,021 set by A'ja Wilson in 2024.

Mitchell is averaging 25.2 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game for the Fever.

More: Fever's Kelsey Mitchell breaks A'ja Wilson's WNBA single-season points record

title: Browns HC Gets Candid About Time With Buccaneers
description: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers offensive coordinator from 2016 through the 2018 season. The Bucs had a lot of success on offense under Monken, but things went sideways and the two parted ways. Now that Monken is a head coach for the first time in his NFL career, he […] The post Browns HC Gets Candid About Time With Buccaneers appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers offensive coordinator from 2016 through the 2018 season. The Bucs had a lot of success on offense under Monken, but things went sideways and the two parted ways.

Now that Monken is a head coach for the first time in his NFL career, he got a chance to reflect on the team that gave him his first real chance at calling plays in the NFL.

"I wouldn't be where I'm at without Dirk Koetter, who was the head coach there," admitted Monken. "He gave me the opportunity to call plays in '18, and that changed my track forever."

LIVE: HC Todd Monken speaks to the media after practice https://t.co/mrudxHgsW6

— Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 18, 2026

Monken gave a lot of credit to Koetter for being where he is now. However, he also noted that he still enjoys catching up with people in the front office that he sees around the NFL. From General Manager Jason Licht to other personnel and front office members, Monken listed off friends that he made in Tampa Bay.

"I consider people in the front office friends of mine," said Monken. "We just didn't win enough, but I really enjoyed it there; I grew as a coach."

The Bucs went 19-29 during the time that Monken was with the Buccaneers.

The Bucs went 9-7 in the first year that Monken was the offensive coordinator for Tampa Bay. However, as Monken noted, he was not calling plays. Was under an offensive-minded head coach who called the plays.

The team went 5-11 in the second year that Monken worked under Koetter. So, Koetter handed the playcalling to Monken. The offense thrived under Monken, but the defense let them down. They went 5-11 again and cleaned house.

Monken was hired from the college ranks. He was the Southern Miss head coach from 2016 through 2018 and was the Oklahoma State offensive coordinator before that. He was known for a high-flying offense, and the Bucs gave him a chance in the NFL in 2016.

After his stint with Tampa Bay, he was hired by Freddie Kitchens to be the offensive coordinator for Baker Mayfield with the Cleveland Browns. Now, Monken will face Mayfield against his old team.

Monken lasted just one year in Cleveland. Then, he went back to college as the Georgia offensive coordinator. He stayed from 2020 through 2022.

In 2023, he was hired as the Baltimore Ravens' offensive coordinator. He coached Lamar Jackson from 2023 through 2025, but when John Harbaugh resigned, the team moved on from Monken.

Now, he is back with the Cleveland Browns as their head coach. Monken is 60 years old, and got his first stint as a head coach in the NFL. His team lost 34-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1.

title: Lions Coach Put on Notice After Historically Bad Start
description: The Detroit Lions are expected to make changes after their Week 2 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson said the team has to do something. Head coach Dan Campbell said that things need to change. The most obvious change that many are pointing to is the potential firing of defensive coordinator […] The post Lions Coach Put on Notice After Historically Bad Start appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Detroit Lions are expected to make changes after their Week 2 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson said the team has to do something. Head coach Dan Campbell said that things need to change.

The most obvious change that many are pointing to is the potential firing of defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.

Former NFL player Isaiah Stanback of Good Morning Football made it clear that right now, if things do not change on the field, they have to move on from Sheppard.

"You gave up 41 points; you gave up some points last week that were unforgivable as well," started Stanback. "Last year, you finished in the bottom half of the league in terms of defensive productivity. Now you are hearing your head coach and your hearing your star defensive player, Hutchinson, both express their frustration with the productivity, or lack thereof, defensively. Something has to change…You can always hear things before it turns into a big storm, but right now you can see the clouds start to brew with the main guys in that organization."

"Something has to change, otherwise they seemingly are going to change it for you" 🤔

—@IamSTANBACK on what Kelvin Sheppard needs to improve for the Lions' defense pic.twitter.com/M3bDz4PJ5f

— Good Morning Football (@gmfb) September 18, 2026

Stanback noted that he is aware that the secondary is shorthanded. However, in the NFL, players are often injured, and teams are always shorthanded. So, it is on Sheppard to make changes that can put his team in position to win. He is not adjusting, and if that continues, they have to move on.

Stanback is not the only person calling for Sheppard to lose his job. Jeff Iafrate of Crunch Time Sports noted that a firing is all but expected after the Week 2 loss. He notes that teams do not win the Super Bowl after games like that.

"The stats are historically bad; it is set up for a firing," said Iafrate.

Vito Chirco of Lions OnSI added on. He noted that every week is proving to the Lions that they made a poor choice.

"Unquestionably, with each passing week, it's become increasingly clear that Sheppard is not fit to be an NFL defensive coordinator," wrote Chirco.

Sheppard was expected to be a rising coach in the head coach ranks. So, to see him struggle like this is a surprise in NFL circles. In media circles, they are skeptical about why Sheppard has gotten so much slack.

There is a lot of talk about the Lions not being the same since losing Ben Johnson as offensive coordinator. However, the defense has also not been the same since they lost Aaron Glenn.

The difference is that the Lions are on their second offensive play caller since Johnson moved on to the Chicago Bears. They did not see success with their first option and found a new coordinator.

Meanwhile, the Lions saw similarly poor results from their defense but kept Sheppard. Now, the team might be looking to regroup on defense a year behind the offense. While Johnson has had more success than Glenn as a head coach, the Lions have missed Glenn more than Johnson as a play caller.

title: Baker Mayfield’s rage won’t be taken out on Browns, saving it for a different opponent
description: Baker Mayfield’s revenge game? Not Week 2 versus the Cleveland Browns. Instead, Week 8 versus Kevin Stefanski gets it
fullText:
Most, understandably, believe that Week 2's matchup between the Cleveland Browns and Tampa Bay Buccaneers is all about QB Baker Mayfield's revenge. While there might be some of that, Mayfield has been more positive, in general, about his time in Cleveland in the ramp-up to this week's game. The former Browns, Carolina Panthers, and Los Angeles Rams quarterback has also noted previously that he grew from his experiences.

While a win would be big for both 0-1 squads, for Cleveland and its fans it might be a little sweeter.

Where Mayfield seems to still hold a grudge is against Kevin Stefanski, his former boss and the current Atlanta Falcons head coach. According to Jonathan Jones, Stefanski's departure is one of the reasons Mayfield's rage won't be on full display this week:

I can understand if you'd expect Baker Mayfield to have extra "oomph" ahead of his meeting with the Cleveland Browns, but multiple Tampa Bay Buccaneers sources tell me they have seen no change in his demeanor this week before facing his old team.

Mayfield has already faced his former team, in 2022 when he was with Carolina. This game isn't in Cleveland. If you're looking for a little extra from him, Week 8 against the Falcons, led by former Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski, is the one to keep an eye on.

Perhaps Mayfield and Stefanski didn't have a great working relationship during their time together, or maybe Mayfield believes that his former head coach and play caller was the one who pushed for the Deshaun Watson trade. We know for sure that, according to Mayfield, Stefanski not texting or calling him after he was traded to the Panthers still lingers.

Are you surprised that Mayfield is at peace with the Browns organization? Besides the lack of text/call, why do you think he holds such ill will towards Stefanski?

title: Villa's New Faces Come to the Fore as Emery's Side Finally Gets Off the Mark at Spurs
description: Dan Bardell reflects on Aston Villa's 3-2 victory at Tottenham, with Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson and Zion Suzuki among the new faces making their mark as Unai Emery's reshaped side finally secured the Premier League victory it desperately needed.
fullText:
Aston Villa win at Spurs, to get off the mark for the season in the Premier League.

Aston Villa needed a Premier League win at Tottenham Hotspur more than they needed a perfect performance, and while the final few minutes made a game that should have been comfortable far more uncomfortable than it needed to be, there was enough in the preceding 80 or so to suggest that some of the pieces of this new-look side are beginning to fall into place.

Going into the game, I wasn't particularly bothered how Villa got the three points. It had reached the stage where the result had to come first because another international break spent talking about a winless start to the Premier League season would have felt incredibly long, particularly after the disappointment of the Nottingham Forest defeat. Instead, Villa have gone to Tottenham, scored three times and won a game which contained enough encouraging individual performances to make the result feel like more than simply getting off the mark.

It certainly wasn't straightforward from the beginning. Spurs were the better side for periods of the first half and Villa needed Zion Suzuki, who was excellent, to make sure they stayed in the game when the home side had the momentum. There was a double save early on, another really good stop through a crowd of players and a general authority whenever the ball came into his penalty area which is becoming increasingly noticeable. Villa didn't control that opening period particularly well, but sometimes your goalkeeper has to get you through those moments and Suzuki did exactly that.

What Villa did have, even when they weren't controlling possession or creating chance after chance, was a threat in transition which gradually became more prominent as the game went on. Nicolas Jackson worked incredibly hard at the top end of the pitch and Johan Manzambi, making his first start, gave Villa something they have been missing. There were moments when the decision-making could have been better and occasions where the final ball wasn't quite there, but there was an athleticism and directness to Villa's attacking play which Tottenham increasingly struggled to deal with.

Manzambi's goal was scruffy in its construction, but I actually liked what it told us about him. He's playing as the number 10 but he wasn't standing on the edge of the penalty area admiring the situation; he had got himself into an area where he could sniff out a goal when the ball broke his way. For a 20-year-old making his first Premier League start, there was very little about him that looked tentative, and while I'll go into his performance in much more detail elsewhere, the most encouraging thing was how naturally he seemed to fit into the level of the game.

The second half was when Villa really started to look dangerous. Tottenham had to chase the game and inevitably left more space, but Villa still had to exploit it and for a period Jackson and Manzambi were causing them enormous problems. Jackson eventually got the goal his performance deserved, his first in the Premier League for Villa, and there were numerous examples before that of the qualities he gives this team. He can stretch a defence, he can run into the channels and he has that burst of acceleration which can turn a fairly innocuous situation into something dangerous very quickly. The relationship between him and Manzambi was particularly encouraging because Villa suddenly had two players capable of hurting Tottenham in different ways but operating in close enough proximity to combine.

Then Emi Buendía did what Emi Buendía does. I didn't think he had been particularly good in the first half and I've been critical of elements of his game this season, but I've also always said that he has the ability to produce a moment and his goal was exactly that. It was a brilliant strike and, once it went in, you could almost see the confidence flow through him. There is never really a question about his work rate or how much playing for Villa means to him, and even on an afternoon when everything hadn't come off with the ball, he still found a way to make a decisive contribution.

There were important performances at the other end as well. Tyrone Mings was very good for the majority of the afternoon and Villa needed that because this remains a team trying to establish a new hierarchy after so much change. Mings and John McGinn are incredibly important in that respect. There are younger players in the side, there are new players still learning exactly what Emery wants from them and there are others who may eventually develop into the organisers and leaders Villa need, but at this point those two are still fundamental to holding everything together. Mings dealt with so much of what came into the penalty area and I also thought some of his work in possession was excellent.

That is why the final stages were frustrating. At 3-0 the game should have been dead and Villa allowed Tottenham to make the scoreline far closer than it needed to be. The second goal in particular leaves a sour taste because game management has already been a talking point this season and there is clearly still work to do in terms of controlling matches when the momentum begins to change. The full-back areas were difficult for Villa for much of the afternoon as well, particularly in the first half, and this certainly wasn't a performance without flaws.

But those are things Villa can work on after a victory rather than spending another fortnight trying to explain why they haven't won a Premier League game. That distinction is important. This is a team which has undergone considerable change and there are combinations that are only beginning to develop, players still adapting to their surroundings and a manager working out exactly what his strongest version of this side looks like.

For the first time in the league this season, though, we saw enough of the upside to understand what that version might eventually become. Suzuki kept Villa in it when Tottenham were on top, Manzambi announced himself properly, Jackson gave Spurs problems throughout, Buendía produced the moment he is always capable of producing and the experience of players such as Mings and McGinn remained important around them.

The two late goals mean nobody should pretend everything has suddenly been solved, but Villa didn't need everything solved at Tottenham. They needed a win, they needed some of the new players to begin showing why they were brought to the football club and they needed something positive to take into the international break.

fullText:
There were significant questions facing Green Bay Packers former first-round pick Matthew Golden entering his second NFL season. While Golden did not show many signs of life in his rookie year, his Week 1 performance has already got fantasy football analysts excited about his potential in 2026.

Heading into Week 2, Golden is becoming one of the biggest risers in the fantasy football landscape.

Eric Moody of ESPN previewed the game, and his biggest takeaway is that the Packers wide receiver should be in for a big game.

"Love threw for 387 yards — the second-most of his career — in Week 1 and attempted 42 passes," wrote Moody. "Green Bay struggled to run the ball without RB Josh Jacobs (commissioner exempt list), and its offensive line ranked 25th in run block win rate (71.5%). The Packers would be wise to continue leaning on the passing game, benefiting Love, Christian Watson, and Matthew Golden."

The Packers leaned on Golden in Week 1, and he produced six catches for 95 yards. Still, it was not just the raw production. Matthew Berry of Fantasy Life noted that the metrcis behind Golden's production suggest he is a player who can continue to thrive in fantasy football.

"In Week 1, Matthew Golden led the Packers in both target share (30%) and route participation (87%)," added Berry. "The Packers won't have 42 pass attempts in most games, but his usage was significantly better than what we saw from Jayden Reed.
Golden is the WR2 you want in Green Bay. And might be the WR1A (I'm still a huge Christian Watson believer)."

Watson produced six catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1. So, Golden cannot quite dethrone him for the top spot.

Still, Golden was targeted 12 times while Watson was targeted eight. Meanwhile, Jayden Reed was targeted seven times and caught just three passes.

Watson was more efficient in Week 1, but as Berry notes, if Golden keeps getting work like that, he will be argued the top threat in Green Bay.

Golden did not produce out of the gate with 361 yards as a rookie. He averaged just 25.8 yards per game. However, the Packers had both Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks last year. Doubs is with the New England Patriots, and Wicks is with the Philadelphia Eagles now.

Watson and Reed were hurt last year, so Golden had chances to step up as a rookie. However, the team drafted Golden to replace Doubs and Wicks, not complement them. He was miscast in his role and did not fit into the offense.

Golden was averaging 1.53 yards per route run as a rookie. In one week, his yards per route run is up to 2.38. So he is more efficient when he is seeing the field.

The optimists for Golden were correct after one week. We will see if Golden can string it together for multiple games.

title: Latest impressive defensive performance helps undefeated Cedar Ridge stuff Rouse
description: After allowing nearly 40 points per game last year, Cedar Ridge's defense has dominated so far this season. The Raiders are 4-0 for the first time since 2017.
fullText:
Hours before Cedar Ridge's homecoming game Friday night against Rouse, defensive tackle Jeremiah Passmore promised himself that he was going to record a sack.

"Just manifesting," Passmore said of the self-made vow. "Got to manifest every game because last year I didn't really get to play at my full potential."

The 6-foot-3 lineman netted 1½ sacks, a forced fumble and three tackles for loss at the Kelly Reeves Athletic Center, as the Raiders defeated Rouse 34-16 to move to 4-0 on the season for the first time since 2017, when Cedar Ridge won a district title.

Friday marked another dominant performance for Passmore in a season in which the senior has been a mainstay of the Raiders' drastically improved defense.

"Our energy, we've really come together as a team," Passmore said after the homecoming triumph. "Everybody wants it. Everybody wants to get stops and stuff like that. We've really come together as one unit."

Cedar Ridge's 2025 campaign ended one win short of making the playoffs and with a defense that allowed just shy of 40 points per game. As the season slipped away and opponents kept stacking points, Passmore, who holds an FBS offer from Florida Atlantic, admitted that he mentally checked out.

"I wasn't really getting a lot of TFLs, I wasn't as dominant," he said.

MORE: Round Rock vs Vandegrift score: Dragons win high school football shootout

But things changed when the program brought on Brian Gaylor as its defensive coordinator. The hire of Gaylor, whom Passmore credited with his success this season, helped Passmore shed last year's failures and fully commit to maximizing his final year. The new coordinator has aided a drastic leap in Cedar Ridge's defense, which has allowed 20 points per game thus far, cutting its number from last fall by almost half.

"(Defensive) linemen really make it to where the (line)backers only have to worry about one gap," said linebacker Ayden O'Brien Brown, Cedar Ridge's leading tackler. "The front seven is playing really well together."

Behind the front seven, the Cedar Ridge secondary is thriving. The Raiders have intercepted seven passes this season.

A consistent defense has complemented an explosive offense. After averaging just over 36 points last season, Cedar Ridge is scoring 41.8 points this year, which includes a 21-6 season-opening win against East View that was ended at the half due to weather.

"We talk about a get-it-back mentality on defense," said Bryan Vardeman, the team's second-year head coach. "Our job is to get the ball back for the offense as fast as possible, and give them as many opportunities as we can."

On Friday, against a Rouse squad that had scored 100 points in its previous two games, Cedar Ridge's defense gave its offense plenty of opportunities.

MORE: Anderson football vs Lockhart final score: Trojans cruise to third-straight win

After allowing Rouse to march 80 yards and score on the opening possession, the defense shut out its opponent until the end of the third quarter. In that time, Cedar Ridge scored 27 unanswered points via Dylan Snoga's two first-half touchdown passes and third-quarter scores from running backs Tyler Mutz and Devin Patterson, who recovered a Mutz fumble near the goal line and ran it into the end zone.

After Rouse cut the lead to 27-14 at the end of the third quarter, it began the fourth by intercepting a pass at the Cedar Ridge 32-yard line. But Cedar Ridge caught a break on the next play, when a trick-play touchdown that would have cut the lead to one possession was negated due to a holding penalty.

On the next snap, Passmore broke through Rouse's offensive line and sacked quarterback Chase Whitten, forcing a fumble that was recovered by his linemate TJ Daniel near midfield. Eight plays later, receiver Terrez Harrison evaded multiple tacklers on a 3-yard score on an end-around - his second touchdown of the night - cementing a win that sends Cedar Ridge into District 25-6A play next week against Westwood unbeaten.

Passmore and the Cedar Ridge defense are eager to prove that the unit's performance through four weeks isn't a fluke in district competition, where it will battle regional powers Lake Travis and Westlake.

"We just got to play with a chip on our shoulders and just really, really physical," Passmore said. "That's really it - every drive."

As Vardeman prepared to be interviewed after the game, he spotted Passmore talking with his family.

The coach walked over, and standing next to the star defensive tackle, said, "We're proud of him. He knows that."

title: WNBA’s Rae Burrell reveals the basic way NBA players slide into her DMs
description: Having a max contract doesn’t mean you have smooth game, as Sparks guard Rae Burrell recently made very clear. On the floor, Rae Burrell has quietly put together the best season of her WNBA career.
fullText:
Having a max contract doesn't mean you have smooth game, as Sparks guard Rae Burrell recently made very clear.

On the floor, Rae Burrell has quietly put together the best season of her WNBA career. Even with the Los Angeles Sparks missing out on the postseason, the guard took a massive step forward, cementing herself as a key building block for the franchise.

Stepping into a regular starting role, Burrell expanded her scoring versatility and posted career-high numbers across the board, putting up nearly 15 points per game alongside 2.6 assists and 2.4 rebounds.

She's also hitting her stride late in the year with three out of her last four games seeing 15 points on the box score, as well as two 20-point games.

Sparks guard Rae Burrell recently turned heads by hopping on streamer N3on's broadcast to easily handle him in a 1v1.

Over dinner, she revealed that NBA players frequently slide into her DMs, though she admitted their opening lines usually leave a lot to be desired.

N3on asked: "Do NBA players slide in your DMs?"

She responded: "Yes. I've responded to them before. It just depends on how you come.

He then asked: "You don't have to say a name, but what's like a line you've gotten?"

Burrell said: "Sometimes they just send emojis. One time I got a wave emoji."

With WNBA ratings and viewership hitting record highs across the board, it turns out NBA players are paying close attention, too. But while league interest is strictly professional, plenty of male stars seem to be taking a far more personal approach.

We see the bridge between the NBA and WNBA getting closed day-by-day, as players like Damian Lillard are seen in attendance, while Michael Porter Jr. continues to give the WNBA a platform on his podcast.
